01.4Chapter 1 · Founder · Chapter 1

Why AI Created the FDE

Pichhla section ek shift par khatam hua tha: idea ko working software me badalne ki cost collapse ho gayi. Yeh section is baare me hai ki us shift ne role ko kyun create kiya, use khatam karne ke bajay — kyunki kagaz par use khatam karna chahiye tha.

Implementation cost collapse

Maine yeh collapse andar se dekha hai. Woh builds jinhe main kabhi ek chhoti team ke liye scope karta tha — ek integration layer, ek retrieval pipeline, ek working agent — ab ek engineer coding agent ke saath weeks me nikaal deta hai. Ek proficient engineer use days me kar deta hai. Aur cost girti ja rahi hai, kam se kam initial build ke liye. Is par Chapter 5 me aur detail hai.

Ek obvious prediction banti hai. Agar ek engineer building kar sakta hai, toh customer ke paas kam engineers chahiye honge: unhe software ship kar do aur integrate karne do. Jo hua, woh ulta tha. Sabse capable models wali companies ne engineers ko customer organizations ke andar aur gehrai me daalna shuru kar diya, door nahi. Yeh inversion samajhne layak hai, kyunki uski wajah hi tumhari job description hai.

Jab code likhna bottleneck nahi raha

Jab code likhna bottleneck nahi rehta, toh code likhna value nahi rehta. Jo bachta hai, woh hai sab kuch jo code khud decide nahi kar sakta. Kya build hona chahiye. Kya refuse karna chahiye. Customer ko asal me kya chahiye, uske neeche jo usne maanga hai. Kya woh cheez kisi aur ke data ke against run karna safe hai, aur jab woh galat ho toh kaun jawab dega.

Implementation collapse hui; yeh sawaal collapse nahi hue. Woh concentrate ho gaye — aur concentrate hue us insaan me jo customer ki reality ke sabse kareeb khada hai aur call lene ki standing rakhta hai. AI ne is role ko shrink karke existence me nahi laaya. Usne kaam ka woh hissa jala diya jiske liye pehle ek team chahiye hoti thi, aur woh hissa chhod diya jo hamesha se sabse mushkil tha: judgment, wahan exercise ki gayi jahan ek galat call kisi ka data expose kar deti hai.

Second-order effect — bad ideas ka filter khatam

Ek second-order effect hai jo concentration ko aur sharp banata hai, aur most log use miss karte hain. Jab implementation mehenga tha, uski cost ek filter ka kaam karti thi. Bad ideas estimation me mar jaati thi, kyunki koi chheh months ka building fund nahi karta tha sirf yeh pata lagane ke liye. Ab bad idea par act karne ki cost bhi sab kuch ke saath collapse ho gayi hai. Customer use imagine kar sakta hai, toh woh build ho sakti hai, toh koi na koi use maangega hi, aur galat cheez ka demo bilkul utna hi impressive dikhta hai jitna sahi cheez ka demo. Purana filter khatam ho gaya. Jo use replace karta hai, woh ek insaan hai — aur woh insaan tum ho.

Yahi woh jagah hai jahan judgment abstraction nahi rehta. Customer ek cheez maangta hai. Ask ko one-to-one reproduce karna lagbhag free hai — aur exactly isiliye reproduce karna ab job nahi raha. Job hai ek clear sense hold karna ki solution asal me kya hona chahiye, aur pressure ke neeche us sense ko defend karna.

Pressure teen directions se aata hai

  • Customer se: jisne woh cheez maangi hai, dekh sakta hai ki woh buildable hai, aur tumhara alternative use aisa lagta hai jaise engineer use bata raha hai ki woh kya chahta hai; push back karna relationship capital kharch karta hai jo tumne shayad abhi earn hi nahi kiya.
  • Apni company se: jo chahti hai deal expand ho, renewal sign ho, aur reference customer khush rahe — aur unke interests bhi tum carry karte ho.
  • Deadline se: jo fastest cheez chahti hai, aur literal ask hamesha fastest hota hai, kyunki use kisi ko convince karne ki zaroorat nahi padti.

Taste — aur uska failure mode

Isse taste kaho. Har senior engineer ne ask aur answer ke beech ka gap feel kiya hai. FDE ke version ko ordinary wale se do cheezein alag karti hain. Pehli, ground: taste par act karna customer ke environment me hota hai, customer ke stakeholders ke saamne, customer ka data stake par hota hai, aur peeche chhupne ke liye koi senior nahi hota. Dusri, accountability: tum is baare me opinion hold nahi kar sakte ki kya build hona chahiye, aur phir kisi aur ka version fail hote dekh sakte ho. Tumhara call ship hota hai, aur jab woh reality se milta hai, tab bhi tum wahi khade hote ho. Accountability ke bina taste sirf opinion hai. FDE ke paas accountability hai, aur wahi us taste ko pay karne layak banata hai.

Taste ke saath ek seductive failure mode aata hai: contrarianism. Customer ko override karna khud me koi virtue nahi hai. Anchor woh sawaal hai jo Chapter 4 migration work ke center me rakhta hai: customer asal me end state kya chahta hai? Na woh jo usne is hafte maanga, na woh jo tum apne liye build karte. Taste matlab hai unki real destination ko itni clearly hold karna ki tum bata sako ki literal ask kab usse door le ja raha hai — aur woh baat zor se kehna, us moment me jab kehna tumhe mehenga padta hai.

LLM moment — pressure me fold mat karo

Aur tools ke saath ek naya failure mode aa gaya hai. Suggestions ab expert lagti hain, chahe koi bhi unhe hold kar raha ho, kyunki jis model ne unhe draft kiya tha woh expert lagne ke liye hi banaya gaya tha, aur har proposal polished aati hai. Toh is era me taste ka ek hissa yeh refuse karna hai jise main LLM moment kehta hoon: woh instant, apologetic "Oh, my bad. You are right" jo ek model usi moment perform karta hai jab use push kiya jata hai. Customer ke paas pehle se software hai jo pressure me fold ho jata hai. Usne ek insaan ko dusri cheez ke liye hire kiya hai.

Isiliye yeh book how to think sikhati hai, not what to think. Main tumhe kisi engagement ke liye sahi call nahi de sakta jo main kabhi dekhunga hi nahi. Main tumhe woh sawaal de sakta hoon jinse woh call banti hai, aur aane wale chapters unhi sawaalon ke around organize hain. Woh judgment hold karna kya cost karta hai, aur uske aas-paas ownership kitni wide chalti hai — yeh ek comparison se sabse aasaani se dikhta hai. Woh comparison hai founder.

Yaad rakho: Code sasta ho gaya, judgment sasta nahi hua. Galat cheez ka demo bhi sahi cheez jitna impressive dikhta hai — isiliye filter ab ek insaan hai, aur woh insaan tum ho. Pressure me fold mat karo.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Why AI Created the FDE
← Prev01.3 · Drawing the Borders — Flavors of the Role→ Next01.5 · Founder-sized Ownership
01.5Chapter 1 · Founder · Chapter 1

Founder-sized Ownership

Socho ek early-stage founder ek hafte me asal me kya karta hai. Problem dhoondhta hai jo solve karne layak hai. Decide karta hai kya build karna hai aur kya refuse karna hai. Use build karta hai. Ship karta hai. Un logon ke saath baithta hai jinke liye woh hai, sunta hai woh kya kehte hain aur dekhta hai woh kya karte hain, aur result ke liye jawab deta hai — bina kisi upar wale ke jo blame absorb kar le. Paanch jobs, ek insaan, sirf ownership se jode hue. Koi founder ko woh paanch assign nahi karta. Woh exist karte hain kyunki koi aur hai hi nahi, aur unhe split karna unhe tod dega: jo founder apni discovery kiye bina build karta hai, woh galat cheez build karta hai, aur jo founder build own kiye bina discover karta hai, woh insight ko translation me marte hue dekhta hai.

Forward Deployed Engineer founder-sized ownership carry karta hai, ek inversion ke saath. FDE engineering me founder ke sabse kareeb cheez hai: ek insaan jo discovery, scope, build, deployment, aur customer relationship — end to end — own karta hai. Bas farq yeh hai ki jis company ke andar yeh founder build kar raha hai, woh company kisi aur ki hai. Data tumhara nahi hai move karne ko, lekin migration tumhari hai land karne ko. Systems tumhare nahi hain change karne ko, lekin tumhara build unke andar hi run karna hai. Security team ne tumhe hire nahi kiya, lekin jab tak woh sign na kare, kuch ship nahi hota, aur unhe sign karwana tumhara kaam hai. Stakeholders ke apne bosses hain, apne incentives hain, apne doubts hain tumhare baare me — aur unme se har ek ke saath relationship phir bhi tumhari hi hai build karne aur rakhne ko. Tum outcome own karte ho, aur deadline tumhari hai. Is book me sab kuch isi se follow karta hai.

Is stance ko kaho founder's posture: aisi ground par outcome ki full ownership jo tumhari nahi hai.

Surface area — paanch jobs, ek owner

Us ownership ke teen dimensions hain, aur baaki section unhe ek-ek karke leta hai. Kitna hold karte ho: surface area. Har hissa kab shuru hota hai: engagement arc. Aur kiski ground par hold karte ho: turf. Founder ke paas teeno bhi hain. Farq teesre me hai.

Founder ki surface area matlab hai ek saath kitni jobs hold ki ja rahi hain. FDE ka number hai paanch. Discovery: pata lagana ki customer ko asal me kya chahiye, jo rarely woh hota hai jo unhone maanga tha. Scope: use ek commitment me badalna jise woh sign karenge. Build: woh custom software jiski wajah se yeh sab exist karta hai. Deploy: use unki deewaron ke andar le jaana aur trusted banwana ki woh run kare. Aur relationship: woh trust jiss par baaki saare jobs chalte hain. Founder paanchon isiliye hold karta hai kyunki koi aur hai hi nahi. FDE paanchon isiliye hold karta hai kyunki room me koi aur poora system nahi dekh sakta, discovery call se lekar go-live ke baad ke phone call tak. Kisi job ko own karna assignment ka matter nahi hai. Yeh matter hai ki end-to-end context kaun hold kar raha hai — aur engagement par woh tum ho.

Ek real week — jobs lunch se pehle interleave hoti hain

Yeh raha ki paanchon ko ek saath hold karna mere ek recent, ordinary week me kaisa dikha. Jobs calendar par baari-baari nahi aati hain; most days woh lunch se pehle hi interleave ho jati hain.

Monday khula weekly FDE meeting se — mere employer ki, kisi customer ki nahi. Pehle ki jobs me mere daily stand-ups hote the, kyunki tab ek update ek din tak hold kar sakta tha. Engagement par woh nahi kar sakta: jo context main ek project par subah 11 baje hold karta hoon, woh dopahar 1 baje tak change ho chuka hota hai, aur daily ceremony poora hafta drift narrate karne me kharch kar deti. Weekly us speed se match karta hai jis speed se context move karta hai. Baaki Monday us build par gaya jo flight me thi — ek worker, ek aise workflow ke liye jisme PII tha, woh class of constraint jise "What Forward Deployed Engineers Actually Build" aage leta hai.

Building ke through threaded the messages us cast se jiske saath har engagement chalti hai: ek customer success manager jo relationship hold karta hai, ek account executive jisne mere room me aane se pehle meri taraf se promises kar diye the, kabhi-kabhi ek solutions architect ya product manager, aur lately ek deployment strategist jo inme se kai jobs ek saath kar raha hai. Inme se koi mujhe report nahi karta, aur har ek shape karta hai ki mujhe Friday tak kya owe hai. Chapter 3 us cast ke saath kaam karna properly cover karta hai. Point yahan yeh hai: inme se koi bhi meeting nahi hai. Yeh Slack threads, hallway questions, aur quick calls me hota hai, poora din, baaki sab cheezon ke around.

Customer side par, jo conversation matter karti thi woh unki IT ke saath thi — woh setup work karna jo ek worker ko exist karne se pehle unke environment ke andar chahiye hota hai. Aur woh cheez jo slip hui: ek engagement start, ek poora hafta push ho gaya, kyunki unki side par security review khatam nahi hui thi, aur unke environment me kuch bhi enter nahi karta bina uske. Tools jahan hain, wahan hands-on technical kaam us hafte ki sabse fast cheez thi. Slow parts the review, approvals, aur woh ek insaan dhoondhna jo directly responsible ho haan kehne ke liye.

Gin lo, toh split roughly aisa tha: 60% building, 30% meetings aur messages, 10% waiting — aur waiting itni chhoti isiliye rehti hai kyunki blocked engagement wala FDE hamesha ek next build start kar sakta hai. Yahi hai founder's week, transplanted: wahi interleaving, wahi absence kisi ki taraf escalate karne ki, sirf ground kisi aur ki hai.

Dhyan do is hafte me kya nahi hai: ek handoff. Kisi bhi point par kaam kisi aur ki problem nahi banta. Yahi founder's posture hai, aur yeh tumhe ek engineer ke roop me ek specific tareeke se badal deta hai. Most engineering roles ek boundary ke saath aate hain jise tum invoke kar sakte ho: mera code nahi, meri team nahi, mera kaam nahi. Founder's posture woh sentence tumhari vocabulary se delete kar deti hai. Engagement par "someone should handle that" hamesha tum par resolve hota hai. Handled ka matlab personally done nahi hai; matlab hai personally owned: tum woh insaan dhoondhte ho, case banate ho, aur us par tab tak rehte ho jab tak woh close na ho — kyunki agar woh open rehta hai, toh woh outcome jo woh block kar raha hai, woh tumhara hai. Yeh deletion bhaari hai, aur main pretend nahi karunga ki nahi hai. Yeh role ke leverage ka source bhi hai, kyunki jo insaan sab kuch own karta hai, wahi insaan kuch bhi move kar sakta hai.

Engagement arc — har stage order me khulti hai, koi close nahi hoti

Surface area batata hai kitna hold karte ho. Engagement arc batata hai har job kab shuru hoti hai, aur order matter karta hai, kyunki har ek agle ko set up karta hai. Chapters 3 se 10 arc ko dheere-dheere chalte hain; yahan woh speed me hai, ek stage at a time.

  • Discovery: Engagement shuru hoti hai ek aise customer se jisne ek demo khareeda hai, spec nahi. Jo unhe chahiye, woh kahin kagaz par nahi hai. Woh partially un logon ke dimaag me hai jo ek dusre se disagree karte hain, aur partially un workflows me hai jise kisi ne kabhi likha hi nahi. Discovery intent extract karne ka engineering kaam hai — aur yeh engineering hai, kyunki tum jo sawaal poochhte ho, woh is baat se shape hote hain ki kya build ho sakta hai. Chapter 3 ise ek discipline ki tarah treat karta hai.
  • Scope: Discovery understanding deti hai; scope use commitment me badalta hai. Statement of work hi spec hai: done ki ek definition jise customer asal me sign karega, commercial pressure ke under likhi hui — zyada promise karne ka pressure — aur political pressure ke under — jaldi promise karne ka. Number aur timeline usually environment ki poori sachchai jaanne se pehle agree ho jate hain, isiliye Chapter 4 itna time deta hai is par ki jab sachchai aati hai toh kya hota hai.
  • Build: Role ka center, aur "What Forward Deployed Engineers Actually Build" ka subject: custom agents aur workers, unki problem ke liye shape kiye gaye, kisi aur ki problem ke liye nahi.
  • Deploy: Tumhare laptop par chalne wala build abhi tak kuch achieve nahi kiya. Deployment matlab hai use unki deewaron ke andar le jaana, unki security review se nikaalna, unke systems se unke credentials ke under wire karna, aur itna trusted banwana ki woh chale jab tum dekh nahi rahe ho. Chapters 6, 8, aur 9 yahin rehte hain, kyunki yahin par most engagements asal me succeed ya die karte hain.
  • Relationship: Woh ek stage jiska koi start date nahi hai, kyunki woh engagement se pehle shuru hoti hai aur uske baad bhi chalti hai. Baaki har stage un logon ke trust par chalti hai jinhone tumhe hire nahi kiya, aur woh trust chhote increments me earn hota hai aur bade increments me spend hota hai. Uske liye koi ticket queue nahi hai, koi framework nahi hai, aur use delegate karne ka koi tareeka nahi hai. Yeh bhi hai, kai engineers ke liye, is book ka sabse unfamiliar kaam — isiliye yeh ek chapter me fenced hone ke bajay har chapter me thread hoti hai.

Ek cheez jo arc nahi karta — woh hai stage ko close karna. Discovery tab khatam nahi hoti jab scope shuru hota hai; woh go-live par bhi chal rahi hoti hai, jab customer system ko kaam karte dekh kar pata lagata hai ki use asal me kya chahiye tha. Scope har baar reopen hota hai jab environment tumhe kuch aisa batata hai jo statement of work nahi jaanta tha. Har stage order me khulti hai aur khuli rehti hai — isiliye surface area engagement ke aakhri hafte tak badhti rehti hai. Founder ki timeline ka shape bhi wahi hai. Jo kuch bhi unhone shuru kiya, woh kabhi kisi department ko handover nahi hua, isiliye launch tak woh sab kuch hold kar rahe hote hain.

Yaad rakho: Paanch jobs, ek owner. "Mera kaam nahi" wali sentence vocabulary se delete ho jati hai — handled ka matlab hai personally owned, chahe personally done na ho.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Founder-sized Ownership
← Prev01.4 · Why AI Created the FDE→ Next01.6 · Their Turf, Your Outcome
01.6Chapter 1 · Founder · Chapter 1

Their Turf, Your Outcome

Surface area ne bataya kitna hold karte ho, aur arc ne bataya kab. Kis ki turf par hold karte ho, yeh ek alag sawaal hai, aur jawab ek taraf hai. Data unka hai, aur use galat move karna use expose kar deta hai — lekin migration land karna hai, aur landing tumhari hai. Systems unke hain, undocumented aur aise tareekon se load-bearing jise wahan koi yaad nahi rakhta — lekin tumhara build unke andar hi run karna hai, aur production me uska behavior tumhara hai. Security model unka hai enforce karne ko, lekin review pass karna tumhara hai earn karna, aur woh design bhi tumhari hai jo pass karna possible banati hai. Tools unke hain approve karne ko; tum wohi use karke build karte ho jo woh allow karte hain, jo tum choose karte woh nahi — aur result phir bhi excellent hona chahiye. Conventions, history, org chart, politics: sab unka hai, aur tumhari delivery un sab me survive karni hai. Ho sakta hai tum kabhi unki building me kadam hi na rakho, aur phir bhi tum poora din unki deewaron ke andar ho: unka tenant, unka VPN, unka Slack, unke credentials decide karte hain ki tum dekh bhi kya sakte ho. Discovery aur scope bhi — do stages jo tumhari lagti hain — unke stakeholders ke calendars par chalti hain aur unki procurement ke under sign hoti hain. Kuch bhi tumhara nahi hai, sirf woh hissa chhod kar jahan use kaam karna hai.

Mess hi mandate hai

Poori list ek complaint jaisi lag sakti hai. Yeh ek job description hai. Missing control, missing context, missing authority: customer exactly inhi ko absorb karne ke liye ek competent insaan ko pay kar raha hai, kyunki agar environment clean, documented, aur ek insaan ke full control me hota, toh unhe tumhari zaroorat hi nahi hoti. Unke apne engineers use pehle hi kar chuke hote. Mess hi mandate hai. Apne environment par full control rakhne wala engineer valuable hai. Bina control ke outcome produce karne wala engineer rare hai, aur in dono engineers ke beech ka gap hi woh hai jise yeh book train karti hai. Ownership without control. Yahi discipline hai, aur yahin par founder comparison finally toot-ti hai: founder ki ownership control ke saath aati hai, aur FDE ki kabhi nahi aati. Founder's posture wohi hai jo ownership without control ko day to day practice karna dikhta hai.

Do failure modes — dono se bacho

Jo engineers is distinction ko internalize nahi karte, woh do directions me se ek me fail hote hain, aur tum job par dono se miloge.

  • Pehla: turf se ladta hai. Woh conventions se argue karta hai, security review se resent karta hai, un systems ko replace karne ke liye campaign karta hai jo uske replace karne ke nahi hain, aur poora engagement kisi aur ki company ko aisi ground me convert karne me kharch kar deta hai jo woh control kar sake. Woh aksar technically sahi hota hai aur phir bhi haar jata hai, kyunki customer ne koi critic hire nahi kiya tha, aur turf par har ladai woh trust kharch karti hai jiss par outcome chalta hai.
  • Dusra: passive ho jata hai. Woh "no control" ko "no responsibility" padhta hai, ticket ke letter tak shrink ho jata hai, aur wait karta hai ki customer use bataye aage kya karna hai. Woh kaam karne me pleasant hota hai aur kuch deliver nahi karta, kyunki customer articulate hi nahi kar sakta aage kya karna hai; woh inability hi wajah hai ki yeh role exist karta hai.

Teesra path

Jo posture yeh book sikhati hai, woh teesra path hai: ground ko jaisa hai waisa accept karo, outcome ko phir bhi apna hold karo, aur har move ko is baat se judge karo ki kya woh customer ko uski destination tak le jata hai. Is baat se nahi ki kya woh tumhari apni turf par sahi move hota. Tumhari apni turf hai hi nahi. Tumhare paas unki turf hai aur tumhara outcome hai, aur job ki poori skill isi pairing me rehti hai.

Yaad rakho: Founder ko ownership ke saath control milta hai; FDE ko kabhi nahi milta. Na turf se lado, na passive ho jao — ground accept karo, outcome apna rakho.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Their Turf, Your Outcome
← Prev01.5 · Founder-sized Ownership→ Next01.7 · What FDEs Actually Build
01.7Chapter 1 · Founder · Chapter 1

What FDEs Actually Build

Pichhle section ne role ko aisa sound karwaya jaise woh ek saath sab kuch hai, aur ek kharab engagement par exactly wahi ban jata hai. Tum months useful reh sakte ho — tickets unblock karna, integrations patch karna, sawaalon ke jawab dena — aur kuch bhi deliver na karna jo tumhare baad bache. Busy engagement ko real engagement se jo alag karta hai, woh hai yeh jaanna ki baaki paanch jobs me se kaunsi job ke liye baaki sab exist karte hain. Build: custom agents aur workers, customer ke systems ke andar working software. Discovery, data, security, aur relationship isiliye matter karte hain, kyunki woh decide karte hain ki build ship hoga aur survive karega ya nahi. Build hi woh hai jiske liye customer pay kar raha hai.

Agents vs workers — model driver hai ya component?

Build ke do shapes hain: agents aur workers. Industry ne abhi tak settle nahi kiya hai ki kise kya kehna hai. Company ke hisaab se wahi software kabhi agent, kabhi assistant, kabhi copilot, kabhi automation, ya kabhi pipeline kahlata hai — aur ek hi meeting me do log same word se alag matlab nikaal sakte hain. Toh yeh raha is book me in words ka matlab, aur yeh matlab har chapter me yahi rahega.

  • Agents woh software hain jo run time par apna agla step decide karne ke liye model use karte hain. Neeche koi fixed logic nahi hai; model hi logic hai. Agent situation padhta hai, tool pick karta hai, act karta hai, result padhta hai, aur phir se pick karta hai — aur canonical shape investigative hai: aisi cheez jisse poochha ja sake ki launch ko kya block kar raha hai, aur woh systems ke across jaakar pata laga le, bina kisi human ke route script kiye.
  • Workers bhi software hain, lekin control flow fixed hai. Ek defined job, har baar same tareeke se trigger hoti hai, har baar same steps chalte hain: ek document aata hai, classify hota hai, route hota hai — usi order me, hamesha. Model abhi bhi andar real kaam karta hai — document classify karna, fields extract karna — lekin woh un steps ke andar kaam karta hai jo tumne likhe the. Worker me model ek component hai. Agent me model driver hai.

Chapter 5 in dono ke beech ki line poori tarah khinchta hai, aur un cases ko bhi cover karta hai jahan sahi jawab plain automation hai, bina kisi model ke. Yahan jo matter karta hai woh hai jo dono share karte hain: dono custom software hain, ek customer ki specific problem ke liye design kiye gaye, us customer ke real systems aur real data ke against chalte hue.

Demo vs deployment — "can this run here?"

Tumhare aane se pehle customer ne jo demo dekha tha, woh design se generic tha; demos aise hi hote hain. Usne yeh sawaal answer kiya tha: "kya model is tarah ki cheez kar sakta hai?" Deployment ek alag sawaal answer karta hai: "kya yeh yahan run kar sakta hai?" Aur "yahan" specific hai, aise tareekon se jo koi demo kabhi nahi hota:

  • Yahan matlab hai unka data model, un fields ke saath jo unke admins ne 2016 me add kiye the, aur woh conventions jo unke around grow hui thi.
  • Yahan matlab hai unka identity provider, jahan group hierarchies ek decade ke reorgs ko encode karti hain, aur unka pandrah saal purana ticketing system, jiska API aise fields return karta hai jo current UI display bhi nahi karta.
  • Yahan matlab hai unki permission scheme, jahan agent ko jo kuch padhna hai usme se kuch un logon ke liye confidential hai jo use karenge.
  • Yahan matlab hai unka workflow, jise software ko join karna hai, replace nahi — aur unki failure tolerance, jo tumhari se kam hai, kyunki failures unke customers par land karte hain.
  • Yahan matlab hai unki audit requirements, kyunki enterprise me system ne kya kiya, yeh exactly utna matter karta hai jitna ki woh kaam kiya ya nahi.

Demo ke sawaal aur deployment ke sawaal ke beech ki distance hi kaam hai, aur use close karna hi is book me "custom" ka matlab hai.

Healthcare PII story — access pehle, retrieval baad me

Woh list tab tak abstract hai jab tak uska ek bullet tumhe architecture na badalne par majboor kar de. Ek healthcare customer ko ek worker chahiye tha jo nurses ka handoff work kam kar de, cases ke beech. Stakeholders ne ask ko pehle simple bataya tha: automatic, scalable, affordable, aur ek month ke andar delivered — kyunki deadline us system ki renewal se anchored thi jise worker replace karta.

Phir environment bola. Dozens of alag-alag healthcare organizations same shared database se padhte the. Same tables, same schema, ek hard rule: ek organization ke liye jo context worker assemble karta hai, usme kabhi dusri organization ka patient data nahi aana chahiye. Is build ka ek generic version pehle context assemble karta, aur access controls par trust karta ki kaun kya dekhega — aur most environments me woh kaam karta. Is environment me woh ek breach hota.

Access ko retrieval run karne se pehle filter karna tha, taaki worker ke context me kuch bhi enter hi na kare jo requesting organization dekhne ki entitled nahi thi. Woh single constraint hi architecture dictate karta tha, aur wahi idea ka koi demo use kabhi surface nahi karta. Yeh woh tarah ka decision hai jo portfolio project kabhi force nahi karta, aur use jaldi lena hi farq hai ek worker jo ship hota hai aur ek security incident ke beech jiske saath ek progress bar hai.

Surrounding work ka ratio — build center hai, lekin circle bhi tumhara hai

Build ke around baaki kaam baitha hai, aur har piece ek reason ke liye exist karta hai jo tum pehle se dekh sakte ho. Discovery build se pehle aati hai, kyunki galat cheez ko achhe se build karna sabse expensive failure hai. Data build ke neeche baitha hai, kyunki broken data par grounded agent broken hi hai, chahe architecture kuch bhi ho — aur customer ka data usable banana itna aksar asal project hota hai ki use Chapter 4 poora khud ko milta hai. Security build ke around wrap karti hai: woh constraint jo decide karta hai ki kuch ship hoga ya nahi, usually ek checklist aur veto wala insaan hota hai, aur Chapters 6 aur 9 tumhe sikhate hain ki us insaan ko design input ki tarah treat karo. Aur evaluation build ke baad aati hai, kyunki ek system jise customer kaam karte dekh nahi sakta, unke liye woh kaam nahi kar raha. Chapter 10 use un terms par prove karna cover karta hai jo woh accept karenge.

Aane wale chapters build se zyada pages surrounding work par spend karte hain, aur ratio honest hai. Real engagement par surrounding work tumhare zyada hours bhi leta hai. Ek agent jise koi security team approve nahi karegi, kisi bhi tarah se exist nahi karta jo matter kare. Na woh jo data par grounded hai jo trust karne layak nahi hai. Product engineering se aane wale naye FDEs is ratio se har baar surprise hote hain, aur reason structural hai: product engineering me surrounding work bhi exist karta hai, lekin dusre functions use karte hain. Security ki ek team hai. Data ki ek team hai. Discovery ko product management kehte hain. Engagement par yeh sab tum me collapse ho jata hai. Build abhi bhi center hai. Bas tum baaki circle bhi carry karte ho, aur use carry karna hi woh ownership hai jiske liye tumne sign up kiya tha.

Conclusion — book ka map

Chapter ek aisi job ke saath khula jo kisi ne mujhe di hi nahi thi, aur us reason ke saath close hua ki woh phir bhi meri kyun thi. Beech me pieces the: mandate, jiske liye role jawab deta hai chahe posting par title kuch bhi ho. Engagement triangle, woh three-cornered arrangement jiske andar har engagement chalti hai. Founder-sized ownership, paanch jobs ek saath hold ki hui, order me khuli hui, kisi aur ki ground par. Custom agents aur workers jo sabke center me hain. Aur woh distinction jiss par baaki poori book built hai: their turf, your outcome.

Woh distinction aage sab kuch organize karta hai, aur ab tum book ke map ko ek idea ki tarah dekh sakte ho, baarah chapters ki tarah nahi. Chapters 2 se 4 tumhe unki ground par khada karte hain: woh stack jise tum wahan run karte ho, woh spec jo tum ek aise customer se extract karte ho jo use likh nahi sakta, aur unka data aisi state me jahan kuch bhi run ho sake. Chapters 5 se 10 build ko us ground ke across le jate hain — design se production tak, phir proof tak. Aakhri do chapters career cover karte hain: role me aane ka rasta, aur woh tareeka jisse uska operating model wapas in-house aata hai. Har chapter ground ka ek region hai jo tumhara nahi hai, jahan outcome phir bhi tumhara hai.

Ab tum jaante ho job kya hai. Chapter 2 cover karta hai ki FDE customer ke environment ke andar asal me kya run karta hai: stack. Aur shuru karne se pehle ek promise, is baare me ki yeh book kya survive karne ke liye built hai. In pages ka stack churn karega. Frameworks rename honge, interfaces consolidate honge, aur koi tool jiska naam baad ke chapter me hai, tumhare padhne tak ja chuka hoga. Woh churn priced in hai. Tum yahan woh cheez build karne aaye ho jo decide karti hai ki current stack ke saath kya karna hai, us din jab tum kisi aur ki ground par khade ho, outcome tumhare haath me hai. Usme tools age karenge. Judgment nahi karega.

Yaad rakho: Demo poochta hai "kya model yeh kar sakta hai?" Deployment poochta hai "kya yeh yahan run kar sakta hai?" — aur in dono ke beech ki distance hi FDE ka kaam hai. Access pehle filter karo, retrieval baad me; build center hai, lekin circle bhi tumhara hai.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — What FDEs Actually Build
← Prev01.6 · Their Turf, Your Outcome→ Next03 · Technical Discovery and Scoping
03Chapter 3 · Discovery & Scoping · Chapter 3

Technical Discovery and Scoping

Software ki duniya mein sabse common shikayat ek hi sentence ki alag-alag version hai: "they do not know what they want." Har engineer ne yeh bola hai — kisi product manager ke baare mein, kisi stakeholder ke baare mein, kisi client ke baare mein, kisi manager ke baare mein. Lekin engagement par yeh shikayat ek alag hi weight rakhti hai, kyunki wahan koi safety net nahi hota.

Koi safety net nahi hai

Zyaada tar engineering jobs mein is shikayat ke neeche ek safety net hota hai. Kisi aur ki job title mein "requirements" likha hota hai, aur jab requirements galat nikalti hain, toh miss kam se kam shared hota hai. Engagement par koi net nahi hota. Requirements ek aise customer ke andar rehti hain jo unhe articulate nahi kar sakta, koi document exist nahi karta, aur us khamoshi ko spec mein badalne ki zimmedari sirf tumhari hoti hai. Requirements tumhare dictate karne ki cheez nahi hain. Unhe produce karna phir bhi tumhara kaam hai — tumhe hi own karna padega.

Customer requirements chhupa nahi raha

Yeh samajhna bahut zaroori hai: customer requirements chhupa nahi raha. Uske paas requirements hain hi nahi. Uske paas ek demo hai jo usne dekha tha, ek pain hai jo woh feel karta hai, ek budget hai jiske liye usne ladai ladi thi, aur ek picture hai jo uske dimaag mein hai — lekin jis pal tum ek precise question poochte ho, woh picture dissolve ho jaati hai. Poochho woh kya chahta hai, toh woh demo describe karega. Dobara poochho, toh woh batayega ki uske manager ne us meeting mein kya kaha tha jahan budget approve hua tha. Na pehla jawab spec hai, na doosra. Dono jawab evidence hain.

  • Demo ka description — customer ne kya dekha, usse kya possible laga.
  • Budget meeting ki kahani — kisne kya promise kiya tha, kis pressure mein.
  • Feel hone wala pain — asal problem, jo aksar shabdon mein nahi aata.
  • Dimaag ki picture — ek vague image, jo precise sawaal poochte hi dissolve ho jaati hai.

Gap hi raw material hai

Woh gap — jo customer chahta hai aur jo woh bata sakta hai, uske beech ka gap — wahi is job ka raw material hai. Engagement arc ke pehle do fronts, discovery aur scope, isi gap par kaam karne ke liye hain. Yeh chapter us gap ko kuch aisa bana deta hai jiske against tum build kar sako: pehle extraction, phir woh artifact jo use capture karta hai, phir woh proof jo tumhe build karne ka haq dilata hai, aur aakhir mein judgment — kya build karna hai, aur kya bilkul nahi.

Is chapter ka learning objective

Chapter khatam hone tak tumhe yeh karna aana chahiye: customer ki need extract karna jab woh khud bata nahi sakta; use ek statement of work mein badalna jise woh sign karega; ek bhi line code likhne se pehle design review jeetna; aur scoping calls lena — including "kuch bhi build nahi karna" wala call — un commercial aur political constraints ke andar jo tum control nahi karte.

Yaad rakho: Customer tumse requirements chhupa nahi raha — uske paas requirements hain hi nahi. Tumhara kaam us khamoshi ko spec mein badalna hai, aur woh zimmedari kisi aur ki nahi, tumhari hai.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Technical Discovery and Scoping
← Prev01.7 · What FDEs Actually Build→ Next03.1 · Discovery as Engineering
03.1Chapter 3 · Discovery & Scoping · Chapter 3

Discovery as Engineering

Discovery ko aksar soft skills ke dabbe mein daal diya jaata hai — asli kaam se pehle ka warm-up. Yeh soch galat hai. Discovery ek undocumented system ki reverse-engineering hai, aur woh system hai customer ka intent. Intent exist karta hai. Kisi ne use likha nahi. Woh un logon ke dimaag mein distributed hai jo ek doosre se disagree karte hain, un workflows mein encoded hai jinhe kisi ne jaan-boojh kar choose nahi kiya tha, aur us gap mein daba hua hai jo log conference room mein bolte hain aur apne desk par karte hain, uske beech hai. Tumhara kaam use un sources se reconstruct karna hai — bilkul waise hi jaise tum bina documentation wale database se schema reconstruct karoge: probe karke, cross-check karke, aur kisi ek witness par blind trust karne se inkaar karke.

Discovery engineer ka kaam kyun hai

Discovery engineer ki hi honi chahiye, aur use kisi friendlier title wale ko delegate nahi kiya ja sakta — kyunki poochne layak sawaal us cheez se shape hote hain jo build ki ja sakti hai. Wahi meeting bina engineer ke chalao, toh tumhe wishes collect hongi. Tum room mein ho, toh feasibility real time mein chalti hai. Log in meetings mein tumhare paas answers ke liye aayenge, bilkul waise hi jaise aaj log ek LLM ke paas aate hain. Wahi caliber apne liye hold karo. Customer ke business ka working sense lekar andar jao, jo sawaal aane wale hain unka andaaza rakho, aur har sawaal ke liye kam se kam do solutions taiyaar rakho.

Is caliber ki ek maintenance cost bhi hai. Product kya kar sakta hai aur kya nahi — yeh line har quarter badalti hai, aur is line par current rehna job ka hissa hai. Real-time feasibility utni hi achhi hoti hai jitni tumhari product ki us din ki knowledge hoti hai.

Real-time feasibility kaisi sunai deti hai

Jab legal ops mein koi kehta hai "we just want it to tell us which contract governs an account," toh tumhe ek saath teen problems sunai deni chahiye. Pehle, retrieval problem: hazaaron contracts, amendments aur side letters ke neeche chhupa hua. Doosra, permissions problem: kaun kis document ko dekh sakta hai. Teesra, yeh sawaal ki "which contract governs" ka unke business mein ek hi true answer hai bhi ya nahi. Sentence simple lagta tha. Uske peeche ka data model sunna hi engineering hai — aur isi liye wahi conversation do alag log chalayein toh do alag specs bante hain.

Pehle destination question poochho

Sabse pehle destination question poochho, aur seedha poochho: jab yeh kaam ho jayega, toh kya true hona chahiye? Industry kya karti hai, demo ne kya dikhaya, vendor kya recommend karta hai — yeh sab nahi. Winning tumhare liye, tumhare business mein kaisi dikhti hai, aur value kahan land hoti hai? Uske baad tum jo bhi requirement extract karo, woh isi answer ke against test hoti hai, aur jo is test mein fail ho jaye, woh noise hai.

Kaam ko dekho, sirf poochho mat

Meeting tumhe workflow ka org chart wala version deti hai. Desk tumhe sach deta hai — aur desk aajkal aksar ek screen share hota hai; zyaada tar engagements remote chalti hain, aur ho sakta hai tum customer ki building mein kabhi khade hi na ho. Phir bhi, shared screen par click by click, insaan ko kaam karte hue dekho, aur tumhe woh steps mil jayenge jo meeting ne skip kar diye the. Jo log ek level upar se process describe karte hain, woh process ko "as designed" describe karte hain — aur "as performed" process design se match karna saalon pehle band kar chuka hota hai.

Artifacts ke peeche bhaago

Customer ke business mein kahin na kahin ek spreadsheet hoti hai jise koi haath se maintain karta hai, ek export hota hai jo koi har Friday chalata hai, ek dashboard hota hai jo kisi ne apne personal time mein banaya tha kyunki official dashboard galat sawaal ka jawab deta hai. Inme se har ek ek requirements document hai jise likhne wale ko pata hi nahi tha ki woh requirements likh raha hai.

Workaround matlab fossilized intent

Ek workaround intent hai, fossilized. Koi do saal tak ek hand-built spreadsheet enthusiasm se maintain nahi karta. Jahan tumhe aisa mile, wahan kisi ko kuch aisa chahiye tha jo official systems ne dene se inkaar kar diya tha, use itna bura chahiye tha ki usne khud ek worse version bana liya, aur tab se woh personal effort se uski maintenance ka price chuka raha hai. Workarounds collect karo, toh tumhare haath mein unmet needs hain — pehle se prioritized, is hisaab se ki har ek kitne pain ke layak tha.

Aur jin logon ke paas yeh workarounds hain, woh aksar wahi log hote hain jinki tumhe laane ke decision mein koi say nahi thi — aur yeh do facts connected hain. Buy karne ka decision upar se aaya, aur gaps unke cover karne ke liye reh gaye. Jo systems unhone un gaps ko cover karne ke liye banaye, wahi poori building mein sabse clear statement hai ki pehle kya build karna hai.

Ask ko decompress karo

Requests aksar problems ke roop mein nahi aati hain. Woh pehle se solutions mein translate hokar aati hain: humein ek chatbot chahiye, humein agentic chahiye, humein wahi chahiye jo demo mein dikha tha. Stated solution ko problem ka compressed evidence samjho aur use decompress karo. Chatbot kaun use karega, kis sawaal ke liye, aaj woh jo kar raha hai uske bajay? Kabhi decompressed problem seedha wapas requested solution ki taraf point karta hai. Aksar woh kahin saste, chhote aur behtar jagah point karta hai — aur use dhoondhna engagement ka pehla taste moment hota hai: pehla point jahan tumhara sense ki kya build hona chahiye, usse aage nikalna hota hai jo maanga gaya tha.

Har cheez ko triangulate karo

Har cheez ko triangulate karo, kyunki kisi ek stakeholder ke paas poora sach nahi hota, aur kai stakeholders ke paas uske contradictory pieces hote hain — poori confidence ke saath. Spec wahi hai jo cross-examination mein survive karta hai. Yeh sab theek se karo, toh discovery ke end mein tumhare paas kuch aisa hoga jo customer ke paas kabhi tha hi nahi: unki needs ka ek coherent account. Abhi woh account sirf tumhare dimaag aur tumhare notes mein hai — aur wahi woh jagah hai jahan specs drift karne jaate hain.

Yaad rakho: Discovery soft skill nahi hai — yeh undocumented intent ki reverse-engineering hai. Destination question pehle poochho, kaam ko apni aankhon se dekho, workarounds ko fossilized intent samjho, aur kisi ek witness par kabhi blind trust mat karo.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Discovery as Engineering
← Prev03 · Technical Discovery and Scoping→ Next03.2 · The Statement of Work Is the Spec
03.2Chapter 3 · Discovery & Scoping · Chapter 3

The Statement of Work Is the Spec

Har engineer ki pehli statement of work se milte hi ek instinct hoti hai: use paperwork samajhna — woh cheez jo account team ko asli kaam shuru hone se pehle chahiye hoti hai. Yeh instinct ek real engagement mein survive nahi karti, toh use yahin chhod do, jahan chhodna free hai. Statement of work, SOW, hi spec hai. Yahi woh ek jagah hai jahan pichle section mein extract kiya gaya intent pin down hota hai, agree hota hai, aur engagement ke dauraan aane wali har cheez ke against durable banta hai.

Apne khud ke product par, ek drifting spec ek sprint ka kharcha hota hai. Engagement par, spec wahi hai jisse paisa, timeline aur dono taraf ka trust anchored hota hai — aur jo version sabne sign kiya, wahi version month three mein arguments decide karta hai. Woh sign karte hain. Tum likhte ho — aur tum use apne liye utna hi likhte ho jitna unke liye.

Customer SOW ko is record ke roop mein padhta hai ki usne kya khareeda. Tumhare liye yeh ek instrument hai: woh cheez jo tumhara time protect karti hai, engagement ko karne layak kaam mein shape deti hai, aur project ko aisa banati hai jisse tum seekho, na ki jo bas tumhare saath ho jaye. Har clause ko apne aagle chhe mahine ke baare mein ek decision samajhkar treat karo, kyunki har clause wahi hai.

Yaad rakho: SOW contract nahi hai. Master services agreement (MSA) ya order form legal aur commercial terms carry karta hai — liability, payment, termination, intellectual property. SOW uske neeche baithta hai aur kaam carry karta hai: deliverables, definition of done, exclusions, dependencies, aur changes kaise handle honge. Month three mein lagbhag har argument ek SOW argument hota hai — isi liye engineer ko, sirf account team ko nahi, SOW likhna hota hai.

Definition of done jo hold kare

Jo definition of done hold karti hai, uski list chhoti hai, aur uska har item is liye hai kyunki uski absence ne kabhi kisi ko burn kiya hai. Done aise behavior ke roop mein likha jaata hai jise customer khud verify kar sake. Internal milestones nahi: "retrieval pipeline complete" customer ke liye kuch matlab nahi rakhta aur woh use falsify nahi kar sakta — matlab woh asal mein unse koi commitment hi nahi hai. Outcomes jo tum control nahi karte, woh bhi nahi: "response quality improves" aur "the team saves time" hopes hain. Hold karne wali definition of done ek person, ek action aur real data ke against ek observable result ka naam leti hai: ek named role ek defined class ka question poochhta hai aur governed sources se drawn answer paata hai, failure behavior specified ke saath. Agar customer use tumhare room mein bina hone ke check nahi kar sakta, toh woh definition of done mein belong hi nahi karta.

Drifts (behta hua)Holds (tikne wala)
Retrieval pipeline completeSupport lead customer ke plan tier ke baare mein koi bhi question poochhta hai aur governed policy documents se drawn answer paata hai
Response quality improvesPachaas real questions ke ek named test set mein se ninety-five percent sahi answer dete hain, jaisa operational owner judge karta hai
The team saves timeFriday export jo haath se chaar ghante leta hai, unattended chalta hai aur subah nau baje tak shared folder mein land karta hai
Handles edge cases gracefullyJab koi governed source question ka answer nahi deta, toh system yeh keh deta hai aur guess karne ke bajay ek named person ko route karta hai

Exclusions load-bearing hain

Exclusions load-bearing hain. Engagement kya nahi karega, woh paper par usse zyada matter karta hai jo woh karega — kyunki jo kuch tum exclude karne mein fail ho jaate ho, woh baad mein contested hota hai, aur ambiguity tumhare against resolve hoti hai. Jo systems scope se bahar hain, jo data migrate nahi hoga, jo languages support nahi hongi, jo workflows touch nahi honge: unka naam lo. Exclusions list likhte waqt pessimism jaisi lag sakti hai. Delivery par wahi "done, as agreed" aur ek aise argument ke beech ka difference hoti hai jise tum jeet nahi sakte kyunki kuch likha hi nahi gaya tha.

Customer ki obligations, dates ke saath

Customer ki obligations bhi andar jaati hain. Discovery ne tumhe bataya tha ki build kis cheez par depend karta hai jo sirf wahi de sakte hain: systems ki access, un do logon ke hours jo legacy tool ko samajhte hain, data ek certain condition mein. Dependencies ko dates ke saath likh do, aur likh do ki jab woh slip hongi toh timeline ka kya hoga — kyunki woh slip hongi.

Data-condition assumption clause

Ek aisa moment aata hai jab data ki asli state us number ke agree hone ke baad surface hoti hai. SOW wahi jagah hai jahan tum us moment ko pehle se price karte ho: scope yeh assume karta hai ki data ek stated condition hold karta hai, aur agar woh assumption toot jaye, toh scope silently absorb karne ke bajay renegotiate hota hai. Yeh clause tumhe utna hi protect karti hai jitna customer ko. Yeh engagement ke sabse nasty surprise ko ek betrayal se ek planned conversation mein convert kar deti hai.

Signature ek diagnostic hai

Poora document customer ki language mein likha jaata hai. Signer tumhara code kabhi nahi padhega. Agar SOW ko interpret karne ke liye ek engineer chahiye, toh woh apna kaam nahi kar sakta — jo hai un logon ke beech ek shared understanding hold karna jo ek vocabulary share nahi karte.

Aur signature khud hi point hai — us moment ko ek instrument ki tarah treat karo. Ek customer jo is liye jaldi sign karta hai kyunki document usse match karta hai jo woh pehle se samajh chuka tha, woh tumhe bata raha hai ki discovery kaam kar gayi. Ek customer jo hesitate karta hai, jo definition of done par walk-through ke liye ek call chahta hai, woh tumhe bata raha hai ki extraction abhi khatam nahi hua — aur woh hesitation ek gift hai: usne misunderstanding ko tab dhoondh liya jab misunderstanding abhi bhi free thi. Signature ki legal force real hai. Uska diagnostic force usse zyada valuable hai.

Yaad rakho: SOW paperwork nahi, spec hai. Definition of done mein person + action + observable result likho, exclusions ko load-bearing samjho, dependencies ko dates ke saath likho, data-condition assumption ko pehle se price karo — aur signature ki hesitation ko gift samjho, problem nahi.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — The Statement of Work Is the Spec
← Prev03.1 · Discovery as Engineering→ Next03.3 · Proving It Before You Build
03.3Chapter 3 · Discovery & Scoping · Chapter 3

Proving It Before You Build

Ek signed statement of work tumhe project dilata hai. Woh tumhe environment nahi dilata — aur ek enterprise mein yeh do alag permissions hain, alag logon se milti hain. Jo log customer ke systems own karte hain, woh SOW sign hone wale room mein nahi the, aur unki consent SOW se implied nahi hoti. Jo log woh systems chalate hain, unhone vendors ko demo lekar aate aur incident chhodkar jaate hue dekha hai. Unka default answer, unki boundary ke andar naye software ke liye, "no" hota hai — aur jahan woh khade hain, "no" sahi default hai: woh pager, audit aur breach disclosure carry karte hain, tumhare jaane ke bahut baad tak.

Environment unka hai, protect karna unka kaam hai. "Yes" earn karna tumhara kaam hai, aur use earn karne ka instrument hai design artifacts ka ek set, jo build karne se pehle produce hota hai: system paper par, us altitude par jis par veto rakhne wale log asal mein kaam karte hain.

Paanch design artifacts

Set mein kya hota hai, woh shop ke hisaab se vary karta hai, aur shop ko padhna skill ka hissa hai. Neeche ke paanch artifacts core hain, aur har ek us sawaal ka jawab deta hai jo ek competent reviewer poochhega — usi order mein jis order mein woh poochhega:

  • Architecture diagram — har component, har data flow, reviewer ke kaam karne wale altitude par drawn. Tumhari internal module structure nahi. Boundary view: kya kahan chalta hai, kya kisse baat karta hai, kya unke environment ke andar aur bahar cross karta hai.
  • Data flow aur residency — kya data unki boundary chhodta hai, kya model ke context window mein enter karta hai, kya store hota hai, kahan, aur kitne time ke liye. Ek AI deployment mein yeh artifact sabse zyada scrutiny khinchta hai.
  • Identity aur credential scope — system kis roop mein run karta hai, kya reach kar sakta hai, aur har grant least privilege kyun hai jo phir bhi kaam karta hai. Ek reviewer jo tumhe khud scope reductions volunteer karte hue dekhta hai, woh baaki document par trust karne lagta hai.
  • Failure modes aur blast radius — system maximum damage par kya kar sakta hai, use kya limit karta hai, aur recovery path kya hai. Yeh ek promise hai jo tum writing mein karte ho, kisi ko trust karne se pehle.
  • Integration points aur load — unki kaun si APIs tum touch karte ho, kis rate par, aur jab tumhara system misbehave kare toh unke systems ka kya hota hai.

Reframe: yeh bureaucratic tax nahi hai

Zyaada tar engineers is kaam ko bureaucratic tax ki tarah experience karte hain, aur tax wali framing economics ko bilkul ulta kar deti hai. In artifacts ke baare mein teen cheezein ek saath true hain.

Pehla: artifact review ko interrogation se confirmation mein convert kar deta hai. Bina document wale reviewer ko tumhari architecture tumse sawaal dar sawaal extract karni padti hai, aur har extraction meeting ek hafte baad schedule hoti hai. Ek reviewer jiske haath mein ek document hai jo uske sawaalon ka jawab pehle se deta hai, woh sirf boxes check kar raha hai. Artifact hi woh difference hai jo review ko weeks mein measure hone wala banata hai, quarters mein nahi — aur engagement par review critical path par baitha hota hai.

Doosra: artifact design ko build se pehle exist karne par force karta hai, aur diagram engagement mein sabse sasti jagah hai galat hone ke liye. Diagram par ek box badalne ki cost ek conversation hai. Kisi aur ke production environment ke andar deploy ho chuke system ka shape badalne ki cost weeks aur trust hai. Jis reviewer ne tumhare data flow mein ek flaw pakdi, usne tum par sabse behtareen price par ek favor kiya.

Teesra: artifact tumse zyada jeeta hai. Tum engagement ke end mein chale jaate ho. System rehta hai, aur use inherit karne wala bhi rehta hai. Design artifacts us handover ki shuruaat hain jo customer ko owed hai, aur unhe review theater ke bajay living documents ki tarah produce karna un habits mein se ek hai jo ek aise engineer ko alag karta hai jise customer wapas bulata hai, usse jise usne sirf pay kiya tha.

Set ko shop ke hisaab se scale karo

Aage badhne se pehle ek judgment note: set ko shop ke hisaab se scale karo. Pachaas logon ki company ko ek page milta hai, kyunki unhe bank ka document set dena tumhe progress ke bajay process dikhata hai. Bank ko full set milta hai, unke template mein, kyunki unhe ek page dena tumhe risk dikhata hai. Artifacts tumhari architecture ko prove karte hain. Unke liye jo weight tum choose karte ho, woh prove karta hai ki tumne room ko padha tha.

Yaad rakho: Agar customer ke paas ek formal architecture review board, security questionnaire ya vendor risk process hai, toh use full set milta hai, unke template mein, pehli review meeting se pehle. Agar tumhara main contact wahi insaan hai jo tumhare jaane ke baad system chalayega, toh ek page, ek call par saath walk-through karke, aur build badalne par revise karke.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Proving It Before You Build
← Prev03.2 · The Statement of Work Is the Spec→ Next03.4 · Translating Between Stakeholders
03.4Chapter 3 · Discovery & Scoping · Chapter 3

Translating Between Stakeholders

Design artifacts architecture review karne walon ko jeet lete hain. Baaki organization tumhari architecture review nahi kar raha hai; woh tumhare scope ko ek saath paanch directions mein kheench raha hai. Kickoff mein andar jao aur room mein agendas gino.

Room mein paanch agendas

  • Economic buyer — woh pay kar raha hai aur use ek return chahiye jise woh renewal par defend kar sake.
  • Operational owner — woh team chalata hai jiska workflow tum badalne wale ho, disruption chhota chahta hai, aur privately soch sakta hai ki kya tumhara build uske logon ka replacement hai.
  • Security aur IT — boundary ke andar kuch naya nahi chahte, un achhe reasons ke liye jo pichle section mein cover hue.
  • End users — copy-paste wala kaam marna chahte hain aur unke paas ek aur tool ke liye patience nahi bacha jo wahi promise kare.
  • Champion — woh insaan jisne tumhe darwaze ke andar khincha, jiski internal credibility ab tumhare outcome par staked hai.

Inme se koi bhi galat nahi hai. Har ek apni jagah se sahi hai, aur project ke unke versions ek doosre se contradict karte hain.

Champion ki kahani

Champion ko kareeb se dekhna chahiye, kyunki champion batata hai ki contradiction aaya kahan se. Champion ne apni hi company ko ek vision becha tha: yeh product gap close kar dega, das guna speed, sab kuch. Vision ne buy-in dilaya, buy-in ne budget dilaya, aur signature ne sabko ek timeline par daal diya. Dhyaan do is sequence ne us room ke saath kya kiya jisme tum ab khade ho. Champion ke colleagues se kabhi poochha hi nahi gaya. Kisi ne "tum is product ke baare mein kya sochte ho" nahi kaha. Unhe bataya gaya "hum ise use kar rahe hain, jao unhe batao tumhe kya chahiye." Champion ka kaam, jaisa champion ne dekha, tumhe darwaze ke andar laana tha, aur exciting part signature par khatam ho gaya.

Jo vision tumhe inherit hua hai, woh ek insaan ki picture hai ki unki company ko tumhare build ko kaise use karna chahiye — aur ab woh goal hai, chahe woh kitna hi stretch kare. Tumhara part wahan se shuru hota hai jahan champion ka khatam hua: us vision ko un sabko bechna jinhone use kabhi choose hi nahi kiya, use trim karna jahan woh oversold tha, aur dono kaam karna jabki champion ki internal credibility tumhare outcome par ride kar rahi ho. Yeh tumhe engagement bhar ke liye ek double role mein daal deta hai: executor, unke system ke andar ek stranger ki tarah, aur advocate, unke interests ko aise hold karte hue jaise tum unke manager ho.

Do naive responses, dono fail

Do naive responses opposite tareekon se fail hoti hain. Sabse loud voice ke hisaab se build karo, toh tum ek stakeholder ke liye deliver karoge aur chaar ke liye fail hoge — aur jin chaar ke liye tum fail hue, unme woh bhi hai jo renewal sign karta hai. Asks ko average karo, toh tum mush deliver karoge jo kisi ko satisfy nahi karta — kyunki asks ek line par points nahi the; woh alag-alag projects the.

Translation: ek design, paanch vocabularies

Working response translation hai. Tum ek design hold karte ho, aur usi ek design ko har stakeholder ko un terms mein describe karte ho jin terms mein woh insaan project ko measure karta hai. Buyer ko: hours recovered aur error rates cut. Operational owner ko: workflow ke kaun se parts nahi badalte aur human loop mein kahan rehta hai. Security ko: boundary, scopes aur audit log. Users ko: week one mein kaun sa pain marta hai. Har description true hai, aur woh sab ek hi system ki descriptions hain.

Translation test ek integrity test hai

Woh aakhri clause hi integrity test hai, aur woh ek design review ki tarah bhi double hota hai: agar tum current design ko saari paanch vocabularies mein truthfully describe nahi kar sakte, toh problem aksar tumhari vocabulary nahi hoti. Design room mein kisi ek ko fail kar raha hai, aur tumhe yeh delivery par nahi, ek conversation mein pata chal gaya. Ise translation test kaho: ek system ki paanch true descriptions — ya design khatam nahi hua.

Yaad rakho: Tum ek design hold karte ho aur use paanch vocabularies mein describe karte ho — lekin woh paanchon descriptions ek hi system ki true descriptions honi chahiye. Agar kisi ek vocabulary mein design truthfully describe nahi hota, toh design hi kisi ko fail kar raha hai.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Translating Between Stakeholders
← Prev03.3 · Proving It Before You Build→ Next03.5 · Pushing Back — Unrealistic Asks
03.5Chapter 3 · Discovery & Scoping · Chapter 3

Pushing Back — Unrealistic Asks

Phir woh ask aata hai jise tum translate nahi kar sakte, kyunki woh unrealistic hai — aur scoping ka hissa use aisa kehna hai. Unrealistic teen species mein aata hai, aur har ek ko alag treatment milta hai.

The askKaisa dikhta haiTum kya karte ho
Cannot be builtCapability exist hi nahi karti, us reliability par jo unke use case ko chahiye, chahe demo ne kuch bhi imply kiya hoKeh do, reason ke saath, writing mein, aur nearest version offer karo jo build ki ja sakti hai
Should not be builtBuildable hai, lekin unke khud ke stated destination se door point kar raha hai, ya unke khud ke data ke against unsafe haiUnke destination aur unke data se argue karo, phir us route ki taraf redirect karo jo destination tak pahunchta hai
Cannot be built by that date for that budgetSabse common species aur sabse negotiableScope, time aur money ko teen alag levers ki tarah negotiate karo, aur result ko SOW mein land karo

Pushback ke rules

Pushback ki craft ke rules hain, aur woh wahi rules hain chahe ask customer se aaya ho ya tumhari apni side se.

  • Jaldi push back karo. Ek "no" ki price har din badhti hai jis din woh delay hota hai, kyunki har silent day consent ki tarah padha jaata hai. Week two mein diya gaya "no" scoping hai. Wahi "no" week nine mein diya jaye toh excuse hai.
  • Unke goal ke terms mein push back karo. "That will not work" tumhari constraint bol rahi hai. "Woh route tumhare named destination tak nahi pahunchta, aur yeh raha kyun" unka goal bol raha hai — aur woh destination question ki authority borrow karta hai jo tumne discovery mein poochha tha. Tum kabhi stakeholder ke against argue nahi kar rahe. Tum project ke us version ke liye argue kar rahe ho jo woh tumhe pehle se bata chuka hai.
  • Ek alternative attach karo. Bina route wala "no" obstruction hai, aur ek enterprise obstruction ke aas-paas se route bana leta hai. Goal tak pahunchne wale route ke saath wala "no" engineering hai. Agar koi alternative goal tak nahi pahunchta, toh woh bhi keh do, reason ke saath, writing mein.
  • Outcome ko SOW mein land karo. Kyunki pushback jo sirf ek meeting mein rehta hai, woh agle reorg mein survive nahi karta.

$30k se $7k tak ka scope story

Ek client costs cut karne aaya tha. Original scope lagbhag tees hazaar dollars ka tha, done-for-you end to end; client ko ek ungli bhi nahi uthani padti. Woh number unke liye kaam nahi karta tha, toh humne saath milkar trim kiya, cut ke baad cut, jab tak woh saat hazaar par land nahi hua. Price ke saath kaam ka shape bhi badal gaya: meri side kaam ke lagbhag ninety percent se girkar maybe fifteen percent par aa gayi, baaki unhone liya, aur unhone ek external partner ko bhi help ke liye laaya.

Yeh ek chhota engagement hona chahiye tha, aur shuruaat achhi hui. Phir Slack channel, hamari main line, ka character badal gaya. Questions leading questions ki tarah aane lage. Asks dheere-dheere bilkul usi kaam ki taraf bleed karne lage jo unhone saat hazaar tak pahunchne ke liye cut kiya tha — ek chhota favor, ek baar mein, har ek apne aap mein reasonable, har ek tees hazaar wale version ka ek piece saat hazaar wale price par reclaim kar raha tha, mere hours se pay kiya hua.

Use khatam karne wali cheez woh document tha jo humne saath milkar author kiya tha. Har ask ko wahi ek jawab milta tha: main sun raha hoon, aur woh SOW ke hisaab se scope se bahar hai. Baad mein change order ke saath support karne mein khushi hogi; current ask ko land karne ke liye, mujhe chahiye ki hum us par focus karein jo saamne hai. Koi dramatic line nahi. Maine use jitni baar kaha, ginne se zyada — aur use kehna kabhi comfortable hona band nahi hua. Scope hold hua kyunki paper hold hua.

Yaad rakho: Change-order line use karne se pehle likh lo. Ek sentence, plain language mein, customer ki vocabulary mein — jo ask ko acknowledge kare, SOW ka naam le, change order offer kare, aur current kaam ki taraf redirect kare. Ek shaant hour mein ek baar compose kar lo, toh woh pehli baar taiyaar hoti hai jab ask raat ke gyarah baje ek Slack thread mein aata hai — jab tum use warna buri tarah compose karoge.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Pushing Back — Unrealistic Asks
← Prev03.4 · Translating Between Stakeholders→ Next03.6 · Agent, Worker, or No Software at All
03.6Chapter 3 · Discovery & Scoping · Chapter 3

Agent, Worker, or No Software at All

Pichle section ke har pushback rule mein ek badi cheez presume hoti hai: ki tum jaante ho uske bajay kya build hona chahiye. Woh knowledge khud ek decision hai, aur har scope ke neeche uska shape baitha hota hai. Line ek baar kheench di gayi thi aur woh yahan bhi hold karti hai. Ek agent problem ke through apna route run time par choose karta hai. Ek worker woh route chalata hai jo tumne design time par fix kar diya tha, model ke saath bounded kaam uske andar karta hua. Dono ke neeche plain automation baithi hoti hai, bina kisi model ke. Chautha option add karo jo koi menu mein nahi daalta — no software — aur tumhare paas poora gradient hai. Scoping decision yahi hai ki is problem ka asal ghar gradient par kahan hai.

Room ka pressure agent ki taraf dhakelta hai

Room ki har force agent wale end ki taraf dhakelti hai. Customer dhakelti hai, kyunki agent hi demo tha. Tumhari apni company dhakelti hai, kyunki agents hi product story aur expansion story hain. Aur tum khud bhi dhakelte ho, kyunki agent interesting build hai aur worker ek Tuesday hai.

Teeno pressures ko feel karo aur unki geometry notice karo: customer, employer, tum. Yahi engagement triangle hai, ab sirf ek diagram nahi jahan tum khade ho, balki har scope decision par forces ka ek live account — aur koi do corners ek hi direction mein pull nahi karte. Phir notice karo ki teeno mein se koi bhi pressure kya mention nahi karta: autonomy run time par free nahi hoti. Gradient par har step up baad mein pay hota hai — guardrails mein, approval checkpoints mein, evaluation mein jise customer believe karega, aur us system ko supervise karne ke standing burden mein jo unke environment ke andar apne khud ke choices banata hai.

Gradient rule

Scoping wahi jagah hai jahan tum decide karte ho ki woh invoice kitna bada hoga, aur deciding rule chhota hai: least autonomous shape choose karo jo customer ke destination tak pahunchta hai. Ise gradient rule kaho; baad ke chapters tumhe is par hold karenge.

Teen sawaal, is order mein

Shape in teen sawaalon se nikalta hai, is order mein poochhe gaye:

  • Kya route har instance par vary karta hai, aise tareekon se jinhe tum enumerate nahi kar sakte? Agar tum flowchart draw kar sakte ho, toh flowchart build karo: woh worker hai ya plain automation, aur woh testable hoga, explainable hoga, aur production mein boring hoga — jo sabse bada compliment hai. Agar flowchart un cases mein explode ho jata hai jinhe tum foresee nahi kar sakte, aur unforeseen ko handle karna hi asal value hai, toh woh agent territory hai — invoice ko aankhein kholkar enter karo.
  • Model judgment kar raha hai ya transformation? Fixed steps ke andar classify karna, extract karna, summarize karna, reformat karna — transformation hai: worker. Aage kya karna hai, yeh decide karna — judgment hai: agent, aur sirf tab jab pehla sawaal bhi wahi kehta ho.
  • Kya yahan model ki zaroorat hai bhi? Ise seriously poochho, kyunki jawab kabhi-kabhi ek join aur ek cron job hota hai — aur tumhare saamne khada customer AI ke liye sign kar chuka hai. Join phir bhi deliver karna, aur kyun, yeh batana, ek taste moment hai. Customer ne ek outcome khareeda tha. Model woh means tha jo woh imagine kar sakta tha, aur tumhari job description yahi hai: is pressure ke neeche bhi yeh clear sense hold karna ki solution asal mein kya hona chahiye.

Kabhi-kabhi jawab hota hai: no software

Aur kabhi-kabhi jawab hota hai no software. Discovery kabhi-kabhi ask ko decompress karte-karte ek aise problem tak le jaati hai jise software fix hi nahi kar sakta: ek agreement jo do teams ne kabhi ki hi nahi, ek report jo koi bhejta hi nahi, ek data-hygiene habit. Ya problem real hai lekin ek baar hoti hai, aur sahi solution ek script hai jo ek baar chalayi jaye, ya ek afternoon ka manual kaam, aur peeche kuch bhi chhoda na jaye. Ya volume itna low hai ki ek system earn hi nahi karta. Jo kuch bhi tum peeche chhodte ho, woh ek maintenance invoice ke saath aata hai jise customer tumhare jaane ke saalon baad tak pay karta hai — aur ek system jo mahine mein ek ghanta bachata hai jabki har quarter mein ek din cost karta hai, woh ek gift hai jise kisi ko accept nahi karna chahiye.

"You do not need software for this" kehna is job mein single strongest trust move hai. Yeh proof hai, aisa jo fake nahi kiya ja sakta, ki tum unke destination ki taraf pointed ho, apne deliverable ki taraf nahi. Iska cost bhi hota hai: billable scope, interesting build, kabhi-kabhi woh expansion jis par tumhari apni company count kar rahi thi.

Yaad rakho: Gradient rule — least autonomous shape choose karo jo destination tak pahunchta hai. Agent, worker, plain automation, ya no software: room ka pressure hamesha right ki taraf (agent ki taraf) dhakelti hai, lekin teen sawaal aksar left ki taraf point karte hain. Aur "tumhe software ki zaroorat nahi hai" kehna sabse bada trust move hai.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Agent, Worker, or No Software at All
← Prev03.5 · Pushing Back — Unrealistic Asks→ Next03.7 · Scoping Under Constraints
03.7Chapter 3 · Discovery & Scoping · Chapter 3

Scoping Under Constraints

Scope aise weather ke andar decide hota hai jo tumne banaya nahi — aur woh weather triangle ke doosre do corners se aata hai. Deadline kisi renewal date ya fiscal year se trace hoti hai, aur asal kaam se uska relation ek coincidence hai. Budget ek aisi meeting mein fix hua tha jisme tum nahi the, environment ki truth knowable hone se pehle. Promises tumse pehle ke hain, aur woh dono corners se aaye: tumhari apni sales team ke, deal land karne ke liye kiye gaye, aur champion ke, apni hi company se approval lene ke liye kiye gaye.

Politics load-bearing hain

Aur politics load-bearing hain: ek champion jise apne promotion cycle se pehle ek visible win chahiye, ek team jo chahegi tum fail ho jao kyunki tumhari success unki reorg hai, ek executive sponsor jo shayad quarter survive na kare. Deadline tumhari move karne ki cheez nahi hai, lekin uske against kiya gaya har promise tumhara hai. Politics tumhari fix karne ki cheez nahi hain, lekin scope ko unhe survive karna hota hai — aur unhe accurately padhna tumhara kaam hai, jo kisi SOW mein listed nahi hota.

Founder ki posture yahan framing se zyada ho jaati hai aur cost karne lagti hai, kyunki scope wahi jagah hai jahan tum apna naam ek number par sign karte ho, ground poori tarah jaane se pehle. Founder wahi decision leta hai, bilkul isi weather mein: constraints jo usne choose nahi kiye, information jo abhi exist nahi karti, aur outcome par uska apna naam.

Sales ek infrastructure hai

Is weather ka ek hissa permanent hai. Ek hissa tum upstream move kar sakte ho — aur upstream ka raasta tumhari apni sales team se hokar jaata hai. Sales woh gate hai jahan se kaam aata hai. FDE role org chart par chahe go-to-market ke neeche ho ya engineering ke neeche, deals sales se aate hain, early promises sales karta hai, aur number un rooms mein set hota hai jo sales chalata hai. Is relationship ko infrastructure ki tarah treat karo. Ek sales team jo tum par trust karti hai, woh tumhe deal mein signature se pehle laati hai — aur sales cycle mein number set hone se pehle bitaya gaya har ghanta ek aisa promise hata deta hai jise tum warna inherit karte.

Trade dono taraf chalta hai: tum unke room mein jo laate ho, woh product ki current knowledge hai — is quarter mein product kya kar sakta hai aur kya nahi, production reliability par, demo ke ambition ke level par nahi. Sales tumhe deals mein jaldi rakhta hai. Tum sales ko buildable ke andar rakhte ho, kyunki product ki stale picture se bechne wali sales team hi woh jagah hai jahan se impossible promises aate hain — aur tum woh insaan ho jo un promises ko delivery par repay karta hai.

Poore job mein sabse sasta pushback woh hai jo promise exist karne se pehle deliver ho, apni hi side ke ek room mein, jahan ek "no" ki cost ek renegotiation ke bajay ek conversation hoti hai. Is loop ke andar scope hone wale engagements ek aise weather se shuru hote hain jise banane mein tumne help ki thi.

Repeatability test

Weather scope ko constrain karta hai. Woh use choose nahi karta — aur jo bhi room bacha hai, uske andar aise kaam ki taraf steer karo jo engagement se zyada jeeye. Default test repeatability hai: build ko aise shape karo ki hard parts tumhare saath wapas aayein — ek pattern ki tarah jise agla engagement reuse kare, ek artifact ki tarah jise tumhari team rakhe, ya ek gap ki tarah jise product khud close karna chahiye. Jo kaam repeat hota hai, woh compound hota hai. Ek project itna one-off ki uske baare mein kuch bhi dobara use nahi ho sakta, zyaada tar waqt jitna time woh cost karta hai, utna worth nahi hota. SOW wahi jagah hai jahan tum iske against engineer karte ho: deliverables ko aise likho ki kam se kam ek deliverable is customer se aage durable ho.

Engagement lene ki paanch reasons — is order mein

Zyaada tar waqt "always" nahi hota. Kuch one-off engagements us cheez ke liye worth hote hain jo woh contract se aage return karte hain, aur sign karne se pehle tumhe naam lena aana chahiye ki kaun si reason operate kar rahi hai. Order mein:

  • 1. Repeatable work — ek pattern ya artifact jo tum agle engagement mein le jaate ho.
  • 2. Ek net-new product opportunity — ek gap jo is customer ne expose kiya aur product ko har agle customer ke liye close karna chahiye.
  • 3. High ARR — contract apne hi terms par worth hai.
  • 4. Ek user story jis par brand khada ho sake — ek naam ya ek outcome jo agle das deals bechne mein help kare.
  • 5. Future growth — customer ek hypergrowth curve mein early hai, ya tumhari company bade competitors ke against nayi player hai aur use ground chahiye, toh beachhead abhi lo.

Order mein logic hai. Pehle do tumhare haathon mein compound hote hain, iske baad ke har engagement par. Aakhri teen tumhari company ki reasons hain, aur woh real hain — lekin jab unme se koi ek justification ho, toh use jaano, internally kaho, aur one-off cost ko zor se price karo. Jo engagement in paanch mein se ek ko bhi check nahi karta, woh lene ke against argue karne wala engagement hai.

Do poles: over-promise aur sandbag

Kaam kitna bhi achha choose ho, promise khud do poles par fail hota hai, aur tumhe dono ka pull feel karna aana chahiye. Pehla pole over-promise hai: ask ke hisaab se scope, plus pressure, minus risks jinhe kickoff glow mein koi sunna nahi chahta. Yeh momentum jaisa lagta hai aur yeh ek loan hai — trust ke against borrow kiya hua, delivery par interest ke saath repay hota hai. Repayment aise aata hai: data sabke admit karne se worse nikla, aur timeline slip ho gayi. Apne career ke early mein tum yeh loan kam se kam ek baar loge, kyunki tum un cheezon par agree karoge jin par tumhe push back karna chahiye tha.

Doosra pole sandbag hai: itna defensively scope karo ki kuch meaningful promise hi na ho. Yeh prudence jaisa lagta hai aur yeh ek alag failure hai. Ek scope jo kuch risk nahi leta, woh engagement ke layak kuch deliver nahi karta, aur deal ya toh mar jaati hai ya uske paas jaati hai jisne moon promise kiya — customer usse bhi worse off reh jaata hai jitna woh tumhare saath hota.

Honest scope ki anatomy

Honest scope do poles ke beech rehta hai, aur uski ek recognizable anatomy hoti hai: destination, customer ke shabdon mein. Route, verifiable definitions of done mein. Risks, named, owners aur consequences attached ke saath — data-condition assumption sabse aage. Exclusions, listed. Unke logon par dependencies, dated. Ek deliverable jo engagement se aage jeene ke liye bana ho, present. Honest scope over-promise se kam confident padhta hai, aur week one mein confidence contest haarna uski price ka hissa hai. Yeh scope ka ekmatra version bhi hai jo month three mein bhi true rehta hai — aur month three wahi hai jab trust asal mein decide hota hai.

Conclusion: scope reality se milta hai

Founder frame ko ek aakhri beat hold karo, kyunki scoping wahi jagah hai jahan woh apna keep earn karta hai. Ek founder bilkul yahi decision leta hai, bilkul isi weather mein: constraints jo usne choose nahi kiye, information jo abhi exist nahi karti, aur outcome par uska apna naam. Zyaada tar engineering careers mein kabhi woh signature nahi mangi jaati. Is career mein woh har engagement par mangi jaati hai, building shuru hone se pehle, aisi ground par jo kisi aur ki hai. Jo scope tum sign karte ho, woh is chapter ki har cheez ko ek document mein compress kar deta hai: intent jo tumne extract kiya, done jo tumne define kiya, architecture jo tumne prove ki, stakeholders jinhe tumne translate kiya, shape jo tumne choose ki, leverage jo tumne price kiya, aur constraints jinhe tumne absorb kiya bina unhe apne liye choose karne diye.

Aur phir scope reality se milta hai, kyunki signature ke doosri taraf pehli cheez jo wait kar rahi hoti hai, woh hai customer ka data — jis bhi state mein pichle chaudah saal ne use chhoda ho. Woh Chapter 4 hai.

Yaad rakho: Honest scope over-promise aur sandbag ke beech rehta hai — destination customer ke shabdon mein, route verifiable definitions of done mein, risks named with owners, exclusions listed, dependencies dated, aur kam se kam ek deliverable jo engagement se aage jeeye. Month three mein trust decide hota hai, week one mein nahi.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Scoping Under Constraints

02Aage ke Chapters · Overviews · Chapter 2

The Deployment Stack — Overview

Early Release note: Ye chapter is Early Release PDF me available nahi hai. Neeche diya gaya overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references (Chapters 1 aur 3) se banaya gaya hai — poori detail final book me aayegi.

Chapter 1 ke map ke mutabik, Chapter 2 batata hai ki ek FDE customer ke environment ke andar asal me kya chalata hai — matlab woh stack jo unki zameen par khada hota hai.

  • Stack ka matlab yahan: woh software aur setup jo customer ke environment ke andar run hota hai — apne laptop par chalne wala build abhi kuch bhi achieve nahi karta, jab tak woh unki walls ke andar na jaaye.
  • Unki zameen, unke tools: FDE unke tenant, unke VPN, unke Slack aur unke credentials ke andar kaam karta hai — yahi cheezein decide karti hain ki woh kya dekh bhi sakta hai.
  • Approved tools se build: tools customer ke approve kiye hue hote hain; FDE wohi use karke build karta hai jo unhe allowed hai, apni pasand ke tools se nahi — aur result phir bhi excellent hona chahiye.
  • Stack badalta rehta hai: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki in pages ka stack churn karega — frameworks rename honge, interfaces consolidate honge, kuch tools gayab bhi ho jayenge — isliye asli skill yeh hai ki jo bhi stack us din current ho, uske saath kya decision lena hai.
  • Map me jagah: Chapters 2 se 4 FDE ko unki zameen par khada karte hain — pehle stack, phir spec, phir data usable state me — aur Chapter 2 is sequence ka pehla kadam hai.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — The Deployment Stack — Overview

04Aage ke Chapters · Overviews · Chapter 4

Getting the Ground Ready — Overview

Early Release note: Ye chapter is Early Release PDF me available nahi hai. Neeche diya gaya overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references (Chapters 1 aur 3) se banaya gaya hai — poori detail final book me aayegi.

Chapter 1 aur 3 ke mutabik, Chapter 4 customer ke data, legacy systems aur migration ke baare me hai — aur yeh kaam itna bada hai ki use apna poora chapter mila hai.

  • Destination question centre me: Chapter 4 migration ke kaam ke centre me wahi sawaal rakhta hai jo discovery me pehle poocha jata hai — "jab ye done ho, to kya true hona chahiye?" — matlab customer asal me kis end state ko chahta hai.
  • Data hi asal project: customer ka data usable banana aksar asal project hota hai — ek agent jo toote hue data par grounded ho, woh apni architecture kuch bhi ho, toota hua hi hota hai.
  • Data-condition assumption: SOW me scope is assumption par price hota hai ki data ek stated condition me hai; Chapter 4 batata hai woh moment jab data ki asli halat number agree hone ke baad saamne aati hai — aur tab scope silently absorb karne ke bajaye renegotiate hota hai.
  • Import ek one-way door hai: Chapter 3 kehta hai ki Chapter 4 import ko ek one-way door treat karta hai aur har fix ko usse upstream push karta hai — diagram par box badalna ek conversation hai, deployed system badalna hafton aur trust ka sawaal hai.
  • Over-promise ki repayment: Chapter 3 kehta hai ki Chapter 4 batata hai ki over-promise ki keemat kaise chukani padti hai — data sabne maana tha usse worse nikla, aur timeline slip ho gayi.
  • Boring in production: Chapter 3 ke mutabik, Chapter 4 yeh establish karta hai ki production me boring hona sabse bada compliment hai — testable, explainable system jo har baar waise hi chale.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 4 — Getting the Ground Ready — Overview
