05Aage ke Chapters · Overviews · Chapter 5

Building Custom Agents and Workers — Overview

Early Release note: Ye chapter is Early Release PDF me available nahi hai. Neeche diya gaya overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references (Chapters 1 aur 3) se banaya gaya hai — poori detail final book me aayegi.

Chapters 1 aur 3 ke mutabik, Chapter 5 agent aur worker ke beech poori line kheenchta hai — aur batata hai ki implementation cost collapse hone ke baad build ka kya matlab reh gaya hai.

  • Agent vs worker, short me: agent me model run time par apna next step khud decide karta hai — model hi logic hai; worker me control flow fixed hota hai aur model fixed steps ke andar bounded kaam karta hai — model ek component hai, driver nahi.
  • Poori line aur edge cases: Chapter 5 dono ke beech ki poori line draw karta hai, aur un cases ko bhi cover karta hai jahan sahi answer plain automation hai — bina kisi model ke.
  • Implementation-cost collapse: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki initial build ki cost collapse par aur detail Chapter 5 me hai — pehle ek chhoti team ke scope wale builds (integration layer, retrieval pipeline, working agent) ab ek engineer coding agent ke saath hafton, kabhi dinon, me nikaal leta hai.
  • Custom ka matlab: dono shapes custom software hain — ek hi customer ki specific problem ke liye design kiye gaye, unke real systems aur real data ke against chalne wale.
  • Build hi centre hai: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki build role ka centre hai aur Chapter 5 uska subject hai — discovery, data, security aur relationship isiliye matter karte hain kyunki woh decide karte hain ki build ship hoga aur survive karega ya nahi.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — Building Custom Agents and Workers — Overview
← Prev04 · Getting the Ground Ready — Overview→ Next06 · Connecting Agents to Customer Systems — Overview
06Aage ke Chapters · Overviews · Chapter 6

Connecting Agents to Customer Systems — Overview

Early Release note: Ye chapter is Early Release PDF me available nahi hai. Neeche diya gaya overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references (Chapters 1 aur 3) se banaya gaya hai — poori detail final book me aayegi.

Chapter 1 aur 3 ke mutabik, Chapter 6 agents ko customer ke systems se jodne ke baare me hai — SDKs, MCP aur CLIs ke through — aur security review ko design input ki tarah treat karna iska core hai.

  • Teen interfaces, title se: Brief Table of Contents ke mutabik, chapter SDKs, MCP aur CLIs ko cover karta hai — matlab agents ko customer systems se jodne ke woh interfaces jo unke environment me survive karte hain.
  • Integration wahi jo survive kare: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki modern FDE ki deliverable me integrations bhi hain — jo bhi interface unki security review se survive kare, uske through threaded.
  • Deploy ka hissa: Chapter 1 ke engagement arc me Deploy stage kehta hai ki build ko unki walls ke andar, unki security review se through, unke systems se unke credentials ke under wired hona hai — Chapters 6, 8 aur 9 isi jagah par rehte hain, kyunki yahin par zyada engagements succeed ya die karte hain.
  • Security review ek design input: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki Chapters 6 aur 9 sikhate hain ki security wale person ko — jiske paas checklist aur veto hai — design input ki tarah treat karo, na ki aakhri rukawat ki tarah.
  • Design artifacts se link: Chapter 3 ke design artifacts me integration points aur load bhi hain — kaunsi APIs touch hoti hain, kis rate par, aur jab aapka system misbehave kare to unke systems ka kya hota hai — Chapter 6 isi substance ko aage le jaata hai.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Connecting Agents to Customer Systems — Overview

07Aage ke Chapters · Overviews · Chapter 7

Grounding Agents in Customer Knowledge — Overview

Early Release note: Ye chapter is Early Release PDF me available nahi hai. Neeche diya gaya overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references (Chapters 1 aur 3) se banaya gaya hai — poori detail final book me aayegi.

Chapters 1 aur 3 ke mutabik, Chapter 7 agents ko customer ke apne knowledge me ground karne ke baare me hai — retrieval aur context — aur data flow aur residency iska sabse zyada scrutinised hissa hai.

  • Retrieval unke apne data par: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki modern FDE retrieval ko customer ke apne data par khada karta hai — generic demo se alag, deployment ka sawaal hai ki "kya ye yahan run kar sakta hai?"
  • Data flow aur residency: Chapter 3 ke design artifacts me data flow aur residency ka artifact sabse zyada scrutiny khinchta hai — kaunsa data unki boundary chhodta hai, kya model ke context window me jaata hai, kya store hota hai, kahan aur kitne time ke liye — aur Chapters 7 aur 9 iske peeche ke substance par deep jaate hain.
  • PII, retrieval se pehle filter: Chapter 1 ka healthcare example batata hai ki access ko retrieval run hone se pehle filter karna pada — taaki worker ke context me kuch bhi aisa na aaye jo requesting organization dekhne ki entitled na ho — ek hi constraint ne poori architecture dictate kar di.
  • Permissions bhi retrieval ka hissa: Chapter 3 ke discovery example me ek simple sa sawaal — "kaunsa contract govern karta hai?" — ke peeche teen problems sunai deti hain, jinme retrieval problem aur permissions problem dono hain: kaun kya dekh sakta hai.
  • Grounding bina, build toota: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki ek agent jo toote hue data par grounded ho, woh apni architecture kuch bhi ho, toota hua hi hota hai — isliye grounding build se pehle ki shart hai, baad ka add-on nahi.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — Grounding Agents in Customer Knowledge — Overview

08Aage ke Chapters · Overviews · Chapter 8

Taking an Agent to Production — Overview

Early Release note: Ye chapter is Early Release PDF me available nahi hai. Neeche diya gaya overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references (Chapters 1 aur 3) se banaya gaya hai — poori detail final book me aayegi.

Chapters 1 aur 3 ke mutabik, Chapter 8 agent ko production me le jaane ke baare me hai — trust, guardrails aur blast radius — aur yahi woh stage hai jahan engagement asal me succeed ya die karta hai.

  • Blast radius, poori tarah: Chapter 3 kehta hai ki Chapter 8 blast radius ko fully treat karta hai — design artifacts me yeh ek likhit promise ki tarah aata hai: system maximum damage me kya kar sakta hai, use kya limit karta hai, aur recovery path kya hai.
  • Trust earn karna: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki deployment ka matlab hai system ko unki walls ke andar, unki security review se through le jaana — aur itna trusted banana ki woh tab bhi chale jab aap dekh nahi rahe.
  • Guardrails ki keemat: Chapter 3 kehta hai ki gradient par har kadam upar — zyada autonomy — baad me chukana padta hai: guardrails, approval checkpoints, evaluation jise customer maan le, aur ek aise system ko supervise karne ka standing burden jo apne decisions khud leta hai; Chapters 8 aur 10 woh poora invoice present karte hain.
  • Failure modes pehle se likhit: Chapter 3 ke design artifacts me failure modes aur blast radius woh sawaal hain jo competent reviewer poochhega — system maximum damage me kya kar sakta hai aur use kya rokta hai.
  • Handover bhi production ka hissa: Chapter 3 kehta hai ki design artifacts aapke jaane ke baad bhi rehte hain — system rehta hai, aur use inherit karne wala bhi — aur artifacts ko living documents ki tarah banana hi woh handover hai jo customer ko owed hai.
  • Deploy wahi rehta hai: Chapter 1 ke arc me Chapters 6, 8 aur 9 Deploy stage me rehte hain, kyunki yahi woh jagah hai jahan zyada engagements asal me succeed ya die karte hain.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Taking an Agent to Production — Overview

Security, Compliance, and Constraints — Overview

Early Release note: Ye chapter is Early Release PDF me available nahi hai. Neeche diya gaya overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references (Chapters 1 aur 3) se banaya gaya hai — poori detail final book me aayegi.

Chapters 1 aur 3 ke mutabik, Chapter 9 security, compliance aur un constraints ke baare me hai jo decide karte hain ki aap ship kar paayenge ya nahi — security yahan aakhri gate nahi, design ka input hai.

  • Security build ko wrap karti hai: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki security build ke chaaron taraf wrap karti hai — jo constraint decide karta hai ki kuch ship hoga ya nahi, woh aksar ek checklist aur veto wala person hota hai.
  • Security review ek design input: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki Chapters 6 aur 9 sikhate hain ki us person ko design input ki tarah treat karo — matlab design hi aisa banao jisse review pass ho sake, review ko baad me ladne wali ladai na banao.
  • Least privilege: Chapter 3 ke design artifacts me identity aur credential scope aata hai — system kis roop me run hota hai, kya reach kar sakta hai, aur har grant woh least privilege kyun hai jo phir bhi kaam karta hai; reviewer jab dekhta hai ki aap khud scope reduce kar rahe ho, to baaki document par trust badhne lagta hai.
  • Data flow aur residency, deep: Chapter 3 kehta hai ki Chapters 7 aur 9 data flow aur residency ke peeche ke substance par deep jaate hain — kya data boundary chhodta hai, kya context window me jaata hai, kya store hota hai, kahan aur kitne time ke liye.
  • Audit requirements: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki enterprise me system ne kya kiya, yeh utna hi matter karta hai jitna ki woh kaam karta tha ya nahi — aur Chapter 3 me security ko translate karte waqt boundary, scopes aur audit log hi woh terms hain jinme design samjhaya jaata hai.
  • Review ke bina entry nahi: Chapter 1 ke week example me ek engagement start ek poora hafta push ho gaya kyunki unki side par security review finish nahi hua tha — aur unke environment me kuch bhi uske bina enter nahi karta.
SOURCESource: The Forward Deployed Engineer, O'Reilly, Chapter 9 — Security, Compliance, and Constraints — Overview

Measuring and Proving It Works — Overview

Early Release note: Ye chapter is Early Release PDF me available nahi hai. Neeche diya gaya overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references (Chapters 1 aur 3) se banaya gaya hai — poori detail final book me aayegi.

Chapters 1 aur 3 ke mutabik, Chapter 10 yeh measure aur prove karne ke baare me hai ki system kaam karta hai — un terms par jinhe customer accept kare.

  • Evaluation build ke baad aati hai: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki evaluation build ke baad follow karti hai, kyunki ek system jise customer kaam karte hue dekh nahi sakta, woh unke liye kaam hi nahi kar raha.
  • Un terms par jo customer accept kare: Chapter 1 kehta hai ki Chapter 10 proving ko un terms par cover karta hai jinhe customer accept karega — definition of done bhi isi logic par banti hai: woh behavior jo customer khud verify kar sake, bina aapke room me hue.
  • Gradient ka invoice: Chapter 3 kehta hai ki Chapters 8 aur 10 autonomy ka poora invoice present karte hain — guardrails, approval checkpoints, evaluation jise customer maan le — aur scoping wahi jagah hai jahan aap decide karte ho ki woh invoice kitna bada hoga.
  • Learnings wapas product me: Chapter 3 kehta hai ki Chapter 10 us loop ko close karta hai jisme jo kuch seekha, use product me wapas feed kiya jaata hai — aur scoping me hi decide hota hai ki feed karne layak kuch hoga bhi ya nahi.
  • Repeatable kaam ka test: Chapter 3 kehta hai ki scoping ka default test repeatability hai — build ko aise shape karo ki mushkil hisse wapas aapke saath aayein, ek pattern ya artifact ki tarah — aur Chapter 10 wahi learnings product me wapas le jaane ka loop close karta hai.

F1End Matter · Interview FAQs

Interview FAQs

FDE interviews (current era) ke liye — role ki buniyaad se lekar scoping aur career tak, 30 sawaal-jawaab. Har jawaab isi book ke concepts par aadharit hai.

Q01 Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) asal me kya karta hai?
FDE customer ke environment ke andar jaakar pehle samajhta hai ki asal me kya chahiye, phir use build karta hai, unki security review se through le jaakar unke production systems me ship karta hai, aur jawab deta hai ki woh kaam karta hai ya nahi. Solutions engineer sirf configuration own karta hai aur support engineer tickets, lekin FDE outcome ko end-to-end own karta hai — pehli discovery call se lekar go-live ke baad wale phone call tak.
Q02 FDE ka mandate kya hota hai?
Mandate woh hai jiske liye job aapko asal me accountable rakhti hai, chahe posting me likha ho ya nahi — outcome, start se finish tak. Koi ise grant nahi karta; yeh outcome ke saath aata hai. Isliye posting padhte waqt title se aage dekhna chahiye ki role asal me kya own karta hai.
Q03 Engagement triangle kya hai?
Triangle ke teen corners hain: employer, customer, aur aap. Employer chahta hai deal expand ho, customer chahta hai woh outcome jo usne khareeda, aur aapke paas aapki judgment, dono sides ke saath aapki standing, aur result par aapka naam hota hai. Teenon corners mostly aligned hote hain, kabhi identical nahi — aur jab woh alag pull karte hain, tab judgment decide karta hai ki kya karna hai.
Q04 FDE ko solutions architect, in-house AI engineer aur consultant se kya alag karta hai?
Solutions architect design karta hai aur build kisi aur ko de deta hai; in-house AI engineer apne codebase par build karta hai jise woh own karta hai; consultant diagnose karke document de deta hai aur production se pehle engagement khatam ho jaata hai. FDE in teeno se ek edge share karta hai, lekin koi bhi pehli discovery call se lekar customer ke production me chalne wale system tak poora kaam own nahi karta.
Q05 FDE role ke teen flavors kaun se hain?
AI labs me FDE frontier models par strategic customers ke andar build karta hai, jahan employer ka corner sabse zyada press karta hai. Product companies me FDE platform deploy karta hai aur woh custom layer build karta hai jo product cover nahi karta, jahan customer ka corner sabse zyada press karta hai. Consultancies aur integrators me platform employer ka bhi nahi hota, jahan aapka apna corner sabse zyada press karta hai. Spine teeno me same hai — mandate, poora kaam, turf, aur outcome.
Q06 AI ne FDE role ko khatm karne ke bajaye kyun banaya?
Jab code likhna bottleneck nahi raha, to code likhna value nahi raha — jo bacha woh hai jo code khud decide nahi kar sakta: kya build karna hai, kya refuse karna hai, customer ko asal me kya chahiye, aur kya kisi aur ke data ke against run karna safe hai. Implementation collapse ho gaya, lekin yeh sawaal concentrate ho gaye us person me jo customer ki reality ke sabse kareeb khada hai aur call lene ki standing rakhta hai.
Q07 Founder-sized ownership ka matlab kya hai?
Founder paanch kaam ek saath karta hai — problem dhoondhna, kya build karna aur kya refuse karna decide karna, build karna, ship karna, aur result ka jawab dena. FDE bhi wahi paanch kaam own karta hai — discovery, scope, build, deploy, aur relationship — lekin ek inversion ke saath: jis company ke andar woh build kar raha hai, woh kisi aur ki hai.
Q08 FDE ke paanch jobs kaun se hain?
Discovery — customer ko asal me kya chahiye, yeh nikaalna. Scope — use ek commitment me badalna jise customer sign kare. Build — woh custom software jiske liye yeh sab hai. Deploy — use unki walls ke andar le jaakar trusted banana. Aur relationship — woh trust jis par baaki chaaro jobs chalti hain. Koi bhi job handoff nahi hoti, kyunki end-to-end context sirf aapke paas hai.
Q09 Their turf, your outcome ka matlab kya hai?
Data unka hai, systems unke hain, security model unka hai, tools unke approved hain — lekin outcome aapka hai. Aap unke tenant, VPN, Slack aur credentials ke andar kaam karte ho, aur delivery ko unki har convention, history aur politics se survive karna hota hai. Control ke bina ownership — yahi is job ki discipline hai.
Q10 FDE turf se ladne ya passive hone ki galti kyun karta hai?
Pehli galti turf se ladna hai — conventions se argue karna, security review se resent karna, systems replace karne ki campaign chalana — technically sahi hokar bhi haar jaate ho, kyunki customer ne critic hire nahi kiya tha. Doosri galti passive hona hai — ticket ke letter tak shrink ho jaana aur customer ke batane ka wait karna — lekin customer bata hi nahi sakta, isiliye to role hai. Teesra raasta hai: ground ko jaisa hai waisa accept karo, outcome ko apna maano, aur har move ko destination se judge karo.
Q11 Agent aur worker me kya farak hai?
Agent me model run time par apna next step khud decide karta hai — model hi logic hai; woh situation padhta hai, tool pick karta hai, act karta hai, result padhta hai, aur dobara pick karta hai. Worker me control flow fixed hota hai — defined job, same trigger, same steps har baar — aur model fixed steps ke andar bounded kaam karta hai, jaise document classify ya fields extract karna. Agent me model driver hai, worker me model component hai.
Q12 Kab plain automation, bina model ke, sahi answer hota hai?
Jab route ko flowchart me draw kiya ja sakta hai, to flowchart hi build karo — woh worker ya plain automation hoga, testable, explainable, aur production me boring. Agar problem ka answer asal me ek join aur cron job hai, to wahi deliver karo aur kyun, yeh batao. Har problem ko agent banane ki zaroorat nahi — model means tha, outcome nahi.
Q13 Taste ya judgment FDE ke liye itna important kyun hai?
Ab literal ask ko reproduce karna almost free hai, isliye reproduce karna job nahi raha — job hai yeh clear sense rakhna ki solution asal me kya hona chahiye, aur use pressure me defend karna. Taste ka farak yeh hai ki yeh customer ke environment me, unke stakeholders ke saamne, unke data ke stake par, bina kisi senior ke peeche chhupe, act hota hai — aur aapki call ship hoti hai, aap wahi khade rehte ho jab woh reality se milti hai.
Q14 Discovery ko engineering kyun kaha jata hai, soft skill kyun nahi?
Discovery ek undocumented system — customer ki intent — ko reverse-engineer karna hai, jo logon ke dimaag me bati hui hai, workflows me encoded hai, aur meeting me kahi gayi baat aur desk par kiye gaye kaam ke gap me chhupi hai. Engineer isliye chahiye kyunki poochhne layak sawaal isse shaped hote hain ki kya build ho sakta hai — bina engineer ke meeting se wishes collect hoti hain, feasibility real time me nahi chalti.
Q15 Destination question kya hai aur use pehle kyun poochna chahiye?
Destination question hai: jab ye done ho, to kya true hona chahiye? Yeh discovery aur migration dono ke centre me hai. Iske baad nikli har requirement isi answer se test hoti hai, aur jo is test me fail ho, woh noise hai. Yeh customer ki apni winning definition maangta hai — industry kya karti hai, demo ne kya dikhaya, ya vendor kya recommend karta hai, yeh nahi.
Q16 Workarounds discovery me itne valuable kyun hote hain?
Workaround fossilized intent hai — koi do saal tak haath se spreadsheet isliye maintain nahi karta kyunki use shauk hai; isliye karta hai kyunki official systems ne woh cheez dene se mana kar diya jo use badly chahiye thi. Workarounds collect kar lo to unmet needs haath me hain, pehle se prioritized — har ek ne jitna pain saha, utni hi uski priority.
Q17 Statement of Work (SOW) asal me kya hai?
SOW hi spec hai — woh ekmatra jagah jahan discovery se nikli intent pin down hokar, agree hokar, durable banti hai. Yeh contract nahi hai; MSA ya order form legal aur commercial terms carry karta hai, SOW uske neeche kaam carry karta hai — deliverables, definition of done, exclusions, dependencies, aur changes kaise handle honge. Month three me almost har argument SOW argument hota hai.
Q18 Definition of done jo hold kare, woh kaisi hoti hai?
Woh behavior ke roop me likhi hoti hai jise customer khud verify kar sake — ek named role, ek defined class ka sawaal, aur real data ke against observable result, failure behavior ke saath. 'Retrieval pipeline complete' jaise internal milestones ka customer ke liye koi matlab nahi, aur 'response quality improves' jaise outcomes aapke control me nahi. Agar customer aapke bina room me hue check nahi kar sakta, to woh definition of done me belong nahi karta.
Q19 SOW me exclusions aur data-condition assumption kyun load-bearing hote hain?
Jo engagement nahi karega, woh paper par usse zyada matter karta hai jo karega — kyunki jo exclude nahi kiya, woh baad me contested hota hai, aur ambiguity aapke against resolve hoti hai. Data-condition assumption bhi aisi hi hai: scope is assumption par price hota hai ki data ek stated condition me hai, aur agar assumption toote, to scope renegotiate hota hai, silently absorb nahi hota.
Q20 Design artifacts kya hain aur review se pehle kyun banaye jate hain?
Design artifacts system ko paper par dikhate hain, us altitude par jis par veto wale log kaam karte hain — architecture diagram, data flow aur residency, identity aur credential scope, failure modes aur blast radius, aur integration points aur load. Reviewer ke paas document ho to review interrogation se confirmation ban jaata hai — hafton ke bajaye quarters nahi lagte — aur diagram sabse sasti jagah hai jahan galat hona affordable hai.
Q21 Data flow aur residency artifact ko sabse zyada scrutiny kyun milti hai?
AI deployment me yahi artifact batata hai ki kaunsa data customer ki boundary chhodta hai, kya model ke context window me jaata hai, kya store hota hai, kahan aur kitne time ke liye. Security aur IT ke liye yahi sabse pehla sawaal hota hai, kyunki unke paas pager, audit aur breach disclosure rehta hai, aapke jaane ke baad bhi.
Q22 Translation test kya hai?
Ek hi design ko paanch stakeholders ko unki apni vocabulary me truthfully describe karna — buyer ko hours recovered aur error rates cut, operational owner ko workflow ke kaunse hisse nahi badalte aur human kahan loop me rehta hai, security ko boundary, scopes aur audit log, users ko kaunsa pain week one me marta hai. Agar paanchon true descriptions nahi ban paati, to problem aapki vocabulary nahi hai — design kisi ek ko fail kar raha hai, aur yeh delivery se pehle conversation me pata chal gaya.
Q23 Unrealistic asks ki teen species kaun si hain aur har ek ka jawab kya hai?
Cannot be built — capability us reliability par exist hi nahi karti jo unka use case maangta hai; reason ke saath likhit me batao aur nearest buildable version offer karo. Should not be built — buildable hai lekin unke destination se door ya unke data ke against unsafe hai; unke destination aur data se argue karke redirect karo. Cannot be built by that date for that budget — sabse common aur sabse negotiable; scope, time aur money ko teen alag levers ki tarah negotiate karo aur result SOW me land karo.
Q24 Pushback ke rules kya hain?
Jaldi push back karo — week two ka no scoping hai, week nine ka no excuse hai, kyunki har silent day consent padha jaata hai. Unke goal ke terms me push back karo — 'yeh route aapke destination tak nahi pahunchta, aur kyun' — apni constraint ke terms me nahi. Hamesha alternative attach karo — bina route wala no obstruction hai. Aur outcome ko SOW me land karo, kyunki meeting me rehne wala pushback agle reorg tak survive nahi karta.
Q25 Gradient rule kya hai?
Gradient rule hai: least autonomous shape choose karo jo customer ke destination tak pahunche. Agent, worker, plain automation, ya no software — yeh ek gradient hai, aur har kadam upar baad me chukana padta hai: guardrails, approval checkpoints, evaluation jise customer maan le, aur ek self-deciding system ko supervise karne ka burden. Scoping wahi jagah hai jahan aap decide karte ho ki woh invoice kitna bada hoga.
Q26 Kab no software sahi answer hota hai?
Jab discovery ask ko decompress karke ek aisi problem tak le jaaye jise software fix hi nahi kar sakta — do teams ke beech kabhi na hua agreement, ek report jo koi bhejta hi nahi, ek data-hygiene habit — ya problem ek baar ki ho, ya volume itna kam ho ki system earn hi na kare. 'Aapko iske liye software nahi chahiye' kehna job ka sabse strong trust move hai, kyunki yeh prove karta hai ki aap unke destination ki taraf pointed ho, apne deliverable ki taraf nahi.
Q27 Engagement arc ke stages kaise kaam karte hain?
Discovery, phir scope, phir build, phir deploy, aur poora time relationship — har stage order me khulta hai, lekin koi bhi stage close nahi hoti. Discovery go-live par bhi chal rahi hoti hai, jab customer system ko kaam karte dekhkar samajhta hai ki woh asal me kya chahta tha. Scope har baar reopen hota hai jab environment SOW ko kuch naya batata hai. Isliye surface area engagement ke aakhri hafte tak badhta rehta hai.
Q28 Scope commercial aur political pressure me kaise decide hota hai?
Deadline renewal date ya fiscal year se aata hai, budget aapke bina hui meeting me fix hua tha, aur promises dono corners se pehle se aaye hote hain — sales rep ke aur champion ke. Scope in constraints ke andar decide hota hai, lekin constraints scope ko choose nahi karte — aap karte ho. Honest scope over-promise aur sandbagging ke beech rehta hai: destination customer ke shabdon me, verifiable definitions of done, named risks, exclusions, dated dependencies, aur ek deliverable jo engagement se aage survive kare.
Q29 Repeatable work ka test kya hai aur one-off engagement kab worth hota hai?
Default test repeatability hai — build ko aise shape karo ki mushkil hisse pattern ya artifact ki tarah agle engagement me wapas aayein. One-off worth hota hai sirf paanch reasons me se ek par: repeatable work, net-new product opportunity, high ARR, brand ke liye user story, ya future growth. Pehle do aapke haath me compound karte hain; aakhri teen company ke reasons hain — jab wahi justification ho, to use internally naam do aur one-off cost ko zor se price karo.
Q30 Sales team ke saath FDE ka relationship kyun infrastructure hai?
Sales woh gate hai jisse kaam aata hai — deals sales ke through aate hain, early promises sales karta hai, aur number sales ke rooms me set hota hai. Jo FDE sales ka trust jeetta hai, use deal me signature se pehle bulaya jaata hai, aur signature se pehle bitaaya har ghanta ek aisa promise hata deta hai jo aapko delivery par chukana padta. Badle me aap sales ko product ki current capability batate ho — production reliability par, demo ke ambition par nahi — taaki stale picture se impossible promises na banein.

Honest out-of-scope list

  • Chapters 2, 4–12 ki poori detail: Ye Early Release PDF (66 pages) sirf Chapters 1 aur 3 poore contain karta hai. Baaki 10 chapters is PDF me nahi hain — unke sirf overviews diye gaye hain, jo book ke andar ke cross-references se banaye gaye hain. Final published book me ye chapters poore milenge.
  • Book ka GitHub repo: Book kehti hai "the GitHub repo will be made active later on" — Early Release ke time par repo active nahi tha. Isliye koi repo link nahi diya ja sakta.
  • Code: Is book me koi code printed nahi hai — na chapters me, na appendix me. Isliye is SPA me koi code blocks nahi hain. Ye book concepts aur judgment par hai, implementation par nahi.
  • Interviews: Is book me koi interviews nahi hain (Chapter 11 interview cover karta hai, lekin woh chapter is PDF me nahi hai), isliye koi interview sections nahi hain.
  • About the Author: Book ke ant me author bio hai, lekin usme personal details hain — isliye use is SPA me include nahi kiya gaya.
